Admission is a separate append-only WorkspaceProposalAdmissionDecision with Workspace-supplied decision identity, proposalId, policy refs, actor/capability refs, current target/projection freshness evidence, status admitted/rejected/blocked/needs-review, issues, sourceRefs, and audit. Missing policy, missing capability context, malformed material, stale/unknown targets, unsupported family, duplicate/idempotency conflict, or required human review fail closed as rejected/blocked/needs-review status material. No matching admission policy defaults to needs-review rather than admitted. Application consumes only admitted, issue-free, envelope-matching decisions and lowers through family-specific application paths such as required-input response, WorkItem spawn, WorkItem link, or WorkItem domain action. The generic application stage may record application status/idempotency/source/audit and refs to emitted family-specific facts, but it is not a universal arbitrary fact emitter. Canvas may expose focused pure preview/intake helpers, but it must not generate canonical proposal/admission/application ids, admit, apply, mutate WorkItems, satisfy input gates, emit link truth, execute providers/runtimes, or promote SidePanelActionIntent into durable graph truth. Raw ready request material, if accepted by helpers, is Workspace-owned boundary material and must not become a broad Canvas root or workspace-intents public API.
rationale: D397-D407 already separate WorkItem spawn, input satisfaction, links, and domain mutations into proposal/admission/application paths. D410-D413 keep Canvas on focused pure projection and intent surfaces, and D418 locks real proposal/admission as Workspace-owned. A generic spine removes duplicated intake/admission/idempotency/source/audit mechanics while family-specific application prevents a catch-all mutation blob. Defaulting unspecified policy to needs-review preserves no-autonomous-decisions, keeps malformed or stale material inspectable, and lets future Workspace policy/admission projectors evolve without changing wave protocol semantics.

layer: L6 / Canvas host renderer event lowering preview / CSP-8 Layer B
question: How should host-registered Canvas renderer events lower into UI navigation, SidePanelActionIntent, and Workspace proposal-intake previews without becoming callbacks, command buses, or mutation authority?
decision: Host renderer events lower through a pure data-only preview boundary. The boundary consumes a WorkspaceComponentHostRendererEventEnvelope plus optional host-supplied visible context such as projection bundle, projection bundle refs, known or stale target refs, actor/capability refs, policy refs, Workspace-supplied ids, requestedBy, workspaceId, and idempotency material. Canvas may emit UI navigation preview, SidePanelActionIntent preview/lowering status, WorkspaceProposalIntakeRequest preview, blocked, invalid, or unsupported-event status material. Event port declarations remain the authority for event name, intentKind, actionId, loweringKind, targetRefs, and lowering status; renderer payload is only bounded data material such as draft input and cannot override routing, name callbacks, request commands, or carry runtime handles. The helper must not call host registries, invoke callbacks, dispatch commands, render React, execute generated source, access providers/runtimes/credentials/browser/session handles, mutate Workspace or WorkItems, satisfy Required Input gates, admit/apply proposals, or emit truth facts. Missing or malformed event ports, non-ready render previews, stale or unknown targets, unsupported intent kinds, malformed payloads, and missing actor/capability/policy/idempotency/projection/Workspace id material fail closed as preview diagnostics. Actual renderer registry lifecycle and UI wiring remain host-owned/runtime-private; real proposal/admission/application remains Workspace-owned.
rationale: D417 defines generated component events as typed data intents, D420/D423 admit only host-registered renderer preview material and typed event envelopes, and D418/D425 keep proposal intake/admission/application Workspace-owned. A separate lowering preview lets trusted host renderers participate in Canvas workflows while preserving package-surface purity and preventing event ports from becoming arbitrary callbacks or a command bus. Keeping payload subordinate to declared event ports also leaves future sandbox/generated-source runtimes with a stable, data-only output boundary.

layer: L6 / Workspace proposal durable spine concrete application boundary / D425 follow-up
question: How should the D425 Workspace proposal spine harden into concrete durable fact vocabulary, admission policy material, application mapping, and focused Canvas helper surface?
decision: Workspace proposal hardening keeps a generic append-only spine with durable fact vocabulary centered on WorkspaceProposalRecorded, WorkspaceProposalAdmissionDecision, and WorkspaceProposalApplicationStatus or WorkspaceProposalApplicationRecorded status material, while all domain mutation remains family-specific. Admission policy consumes proposal record material plus Workspace-supplied decision identity, actor/capability refs, policy refs, idempotency and duplicate evidence, target/projection freshness evidence, sourceRefs, and audit material. Malformed envelope, missing identity/context, unsupported family, unknown or stale target, duplicate/idempotency conflict, missing policy/capability, and human-review requirements fail closed as blocked/rejected/needs-review; no matching policy defaults to needs-review. Application consumes only admitted, issue-free, envelope-matching decisions and may record application status plus refs to emitted family-specific facts, but it must not be a universal arbitrary fact emitter. Required input satisfaction, WorkItem spawn, WorkItem links, and WorkItem domain actions lower through their own application projectors. Raw ready request material remains Workspace-owned intake boundary material. Focused Canvas workspace-graph surface may expose pure proposal/admission/application preview DTOs and helpers; workspace-intents remains intent/preview-only and root Canvas exports must not become a broad mutation/admission API.
rationale: D425 locks the generic spine plus family-specific application strategy, but the next implementation slice needs concrete vocabulary and API ownership to avoid drifting into either duplicated per-family admission logic or a universal apply blob. This refinement keeps shared idempotency/sourceRefs/audit/policy mechanics reusable while preserving D397-D407 family ownership of WorkItem creation, input satisfaction, links, and domain actions. It also preserves D410-D418 Canvas boundaries by keeping intents UI-local, raw ready material Workspace-owned, and focused helper exposure separate from broad root Canvas API.

layer: L6 / Python host API boundary / CSP-7
question: How should the Python host package distinguish no-DATA, protocol ERROR, DATA-level issues, observer failures, context-manager lifetime, and fatal host exceptions without changing GraphReFly protocol semantics?
decision: Python treats None as valid DATA and keeps no-DATA as private presence state. Public Node.cache() returns DATA or raises GraphReflyNoDataError when absent, with optional default-return sugar allowed; it never uses None as a sentinel. Node callback Exceptions become graph ERROR observations wrapped as GraphCallbackError. Subscribe/observe callback Exceptions remain Python observer-boundary failures captured as SubscriberCallbackError. DATA-level validation/domain issues use a future DataIssue DATA envelope, not Python exceptions and not protocol ERROR. BaseException process-control failures such as KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit, and GeneratorExit are fatal host-boundary exceptions and must propagate to the Python caller via a facade/native pending-fatal boundary, not become graph ERROR or SubscriberCallbackError. Graph context managers are real host lifetime scopes: Graph.close()/__exit__ idempotently release facade-created subscriptions/observers and reject later facade use, without emitting protocol terminal/control messages or releasing graph topology as protocol behavior.
rationale: D415 assigns Python idiomatic API, lifetime policy, exception mapping, and value registry ownership to the Python host package while Rust remains the synchronous native engine. R-sentinel requires absence-of-DATA to stay protocol-decidable, so None cannot be the public no-DATA sentinel. D39/R-observe keep observe as read-only egress; observer failures are not graph failures. D359/D270-style DataIssue material is DATA-level product evidence, distinct from protocol ERROR. Fatal BaseException values are Python process-control signals and must not be swallowed by the native callback boundary. Context manager cleanup is host-resource lifecycle, not a protocol TEARDOWN/COMPLETE semantic change.

layer: L6 / Workspace proposal spine concrete implementation shape / D425-D427 follow-up
question: What concrete durable fact and projector shape should implement the D425 Workspace proposal spine without duplicating per-family admission logic or creating a generic apply command bus?
decision: Workspace proposal implementation uses a generic append-only proposal spine plus family-specific application projectors. The durable generic vocabulary is WorkspaceProposalRecorded for canonical proposal envelopes, WorkspaceProposalAdmissionDecision for admission/status material, WorkspaceProposalApplicationStatus for generic application lifecycle/status, and optionally WorkspaceProposalApplicationRecorded for terminal audit material that references emitted family-specific facts. WorkspaceProposalRecorded carries Workspace-supplied proposalId, intakeRequestId, idempotencyKey, workspaceId, proposalFamily, loweringKind, bounded draft material or draft refs, targetRefs, actor/capability refs, policyRefs, projectionBundleRefs, sourceRefs, and audit. Admission consumes proposal records plus visible policy, actor/capability, duplicate/idempotency, and target/projection freshness evidence; malformed, unsupported, stale, unknown, duplicate, missing policy/capability, or human-review cases fail closed as blocked/rejected/needs-review. Application consumes only admitted, issue-free, envelope-matching decisions. The generic application stage records status and refs only; required-input response, WorkItem spawn, WorkItem link, and WorkItem domain action facts are emitted only by family-specific projectors. Unsupported families produce blocked status material. Canvas may expose pure preview DTOs/helpers but must not record proposals, admit, apply, mutate WorkItems, satisfy input gates, execute runtimes, or emit truth facts.
rationale: D425 and D427 lock the generic spine plus family-specific application strategy. This concrete shape keeps shared idempotency, audit, sourceRefs, policy, and freshness mechanics reusable while preventing either duplicated per-family admission stacks or a universal command/apply blob. Making application status generic but domain facts family-specific preserves Workspace ownership of durable truth, keeps Canvas preview-only, and keeps the flow explainable as graph-visible DATA projectors without protocol changes.

layer: L6 / Workspace proposal family application handoff / D425-D429 follow-up
question: How should generic Workspace application status hand off to family-owned application facts without becoming a universal apply bus or losing replay/idempotency semantics?
decision: Workspace application uses a generic application attempt/status index plus family-owned application facts. Generic application status records carry Workspace-supplied applicationId, proposal/admission refs, proposal family, idempotency material, target/source/audit/policy refs, and family application refs only. Family-specific projectors own required-input response, WorkItem spawn, WorkItem link, and WorkItem domain-action facts; each family fact must reference the generic applicationId, admitted decision, proposal, idempotency material, sourceRefs, and audit. Generic projectors may later index terminal family outcome refs and statuses, including recorded, rejected, blocked, partial, repair-needed, or idempotency-conflict, but must never create family facts, mutate WorkItems, satisfy inputs, emit link truth, execute runtimes, or act as an arbitrary fact emitter. Replays are idempotent: matching prior family facts are re-referenced, conflicts become status/issues, and missing family facts leave the generic application pending or repair-needed rather than re-mutating by default. Durable admission material should be recorded before family application consumes it, so family application projectors do not consume preview-only admission decisions.
rationale: D425-D429 lock generic proposal/admission/application vocabulary and family-specific domain mutation ownership, but the family handoff requires explicit replay, terminal-status, and idempotency semantics. This contract prevents the generic application record from becoming a command bus while giving family owners stable coordinates for audit, dedupe, replay, and terminal status projection. Requiring durable admission before family application preserves the preview-vs-recorded boundary and keeps Canvas focused on pure helper material without runtime or mutation authority.

layer: L6 / Python host fatal boundary over Rust batch / CSP-7
question: When a Python fatal BaseException is raised by a host callback while Rust native batch commit is executing, should GraphReFly convert it to graph ERROR, fully roll back the commit, or treat it as a host-boundary abort?
decision: Python fatal BaseException during native callback execution is a host-boundary abort, not a graph value-level failure. Rust native bindings may use a core-recognized HostBoundaryAbort escape marker to tunnel the fatal through dispatcher/wave-owner/batch unwind paths. Wave-owner handling must reset transient wave state and clear stale deferred delivery/boundary work, then rethrow the marker without emitting graph ERROR. Batch body failures before commit retain normal rollback behavior. If the fatal is first observed after batch commit has begun, the implementation must stop further host-boundary work and propagate the fatal to the Python caller, but it does not claim full transactional rollback of already-committed graph effects. No protocol DATA/ERROR/COMPLETE/TEARDOWN, tier, message, ctx, observe, or topology semantics are added or changed. A Python caller that catches such a fatal should discard or close the host graph facade rather than assume reusable graph state.
rationale: D428 requires KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit/GeneratorExit-style BaseException values to propagate to Python and never become graph ERROR or SubscriberCallbackError. D415 keeps Python exception mapping and host lifetime policy at the host boundary while Rust owns the sync native engine. The existing Rust batch design can roll back uncommitted batch-body failure but does not provide a reversible transaction log for arbitrary commit-time callback execution; pretending otherwise would silently add a new batch/core semantic. A narrow host-boundary abort marker preserves D428 without changing GraphReFly protocol semantics or paying the complexity and F-PERF cost of full transactional commit rollback.

layer: L6 / scheduled readiness v1 canonical coordinates / D424 follow-up
question: Which public subject and eligibility coordinates should scheduled readiness v1 expose so equivalent schedule facts do not drift through aliases?
decision: Scheduled readiness v1 uses a single canonical public schedule shape: schedule facts carry subjectRefs only and readyAtMs only. subjectRef and notBeforeMs are stale aliases and fail closed as malformed schedule material rather than being silently normalized. Empty subjectRefs may be represented as an empty array when a producer has no narrower subject, but the field remains present. readyAtMs means the earliest graph-visible clock time at which the schedule may emit ready; deadlineMs remains a separate optional overdue coordinate and does not cancel ready. Domain projectors may translate native vocabulary such as retryAtMs, notBeforeMs, or lease expiration into readyAtMs at the scheduled-readiness boundary. No timer, scheduler, admission, execution, proposal application, WorkItem mutation, protocol tier/message/ctx, or cross-language conformance behavior changes.
rationale: D424 locked graph-visible scheduled readiness but allowed readyAtMs or notBeforeMs while describing the schedule fact shape. In the public API, those two fields are aliases for the same eligibility coordinate, just as subjectRef and subjectRefs are aliases for the same subject coordinate. Supporting both would create replay conflict ambiguity, extra canonicalization branches, and divergent producer habits. A single subjectRefs array and single readyAtMs coordinate keep idempotency, views, status, and retry integration stable while letting domain-specific names stay domain-local translations. This preserves D422/D419 retry/admission ordering, D52 timer-as-source boundaries, and D314-D318 workQueue precedent without making workQueue vocabulary part of the shared readiness API.

layer: L6 / scheduled readiness v1 domain handoff and negative space / D424-D432 follow-up
question: Should scheduled readiness v1 own consumed/materialized, cancellation, or supersession semantics, or should those remain domain-owned handoff material?
decision: Scheduled readiness v1 remains an immutable eligibility projector and does not add shared consumed, materialized, canceled, revoked, or superseded schedule facts or fields. ScheduledReadinessReady and ScheduledReadinessOverdue express graph-visible clock eligibility and deadline condition only; overdue does not mean the schedule was unconsumed, does not cancel ready, and does not execute or mutate anything. Domain projectors own consumption, materialization, staleness, cancellation, replacement, and terminal lifecycle by emitting ordinary domain facts with sourceRefs/provenance to the relevant schedule and ready facts. Tool-provider retry consumes ready by emitting the next ordinary ToolProviderAdapterRunRequested through the existing D419 admission/runtime order; workQueue, workflow, and effect helpers must similarly translate ready into their own admitted/materialized records rather than asking the shared projector to claim, expire, satisfy, apply, or execute. Shared bounded metadata/ref sanitization may be factored into internal or orchestration-local helpers, but no public root sanitizer or scheduler authority is added. Future shared cancellation/supersession requires a separate design review after multiple domains prove identical semantics. No protocol tier, message, graph verb, ctx.up/down, timer, storage, or cross-language conformance behavior changes.
rationale: D424 locks scheduled readiness as provider/domain-neutral visibility over explicit schedule and clock facts, and D432 narrows the public schedule coordinate to subjectRefs plus readyAtMs. Consumed, materialized, canceled, and superseded are not domain-neutral: retry consumption is a next run request, workQueue consumption may be claim or lease-expiration materialization, and workflow/effect consumption may be branch or effect facts. Putting those states in the shared projector would silently turn readiness into lifecycle authority and violate the D424 boundary. Domain-owned materialization refs preserve replay honesty and idempotency while letting each domain enforce its own admission, policy, terminal, and stale-state rules. Keeping sanitizer reuse internal avoids exposing a broad public security/redaction API while still reducing implementation duplication.

layer: L6 / Workspace proposal family outcome owner and repair boundary / D430 follow-up
question: How should family-owned application outcome APIs, completion policy, evidence horizon, replay indexing, and repair flow compose after D430 without turning generic application status into a mutation bus?
decision: Family application outcomes are recorded only by family-owned helpers/projectors for required-input response, WorkItem spawn, WorkItem link, and WorkItem domain action. Generic application status records and indexes carry only Workspace-supplied application/proposal/admission/idempotency coordinates, source/audit/policy/target refs, handoff status, and thin family outcome refs. Completion is evaluated by a data-only family completion policy over visible family outcome facts. Evidence horizon is explicit data that can remain open or close with sourceRefs/audit; a closed horizon with missing or unverifiable family facts projects repair-needed rather than retrying. Replay re-references exact matching family outcome refs and reports idempotency-conflict for same application/idempotency with divergent envelope/outcome. Repair-needed may lower to human-visible repair proposal/review material, but it never authorizes automatic remutation or family fact creation.
rationale: D425-D430 lock the generic proposal spine, durable admission, and family-owned application handoff. This follow-up keeps owner APIs narrow, makes completion and horizon explainable pure projection inputs, preserves replay/idempotency, and prevents repair from becoming an implicit command retry path.

layer: L6 / Python public control facade / CSP-7
question: Should Python expose pause/resume/invalidate as idiomatic public controls, or expose raw Node.up/message sending?
decision: Python may expose host-natural public convenience controls for pause, resume, and invalidate that lower to the existing GraphReFly control-tier behavior through the native dispatcher boundary. The Python public API must not expose raw Node.up(msgs), arbitrary Message construction/sending, DATA/RESOLVED/COMPLETE/ERROR up-going sends, custom message types, or a protocol-tier escape hatch as its ordinary user surface.
rationale: D415 assigns Python idiomatic API ownership to the host package while preserving Rust dispatcher-routed native core behavior. R-ctx-up already permits only control/demand-tier upstream messages, so pause/resume/invalidate convenience is API sugar over existing protocol behavior, not a new tier/message/ctx semantic. Hiding raw Node.up preserves the value-level primary API discipline and avoids reopening structural parity under D24/D32.

layer: L6 / Python fatal facade lifetime / CSP-7
question: After a Python fatal BaseException crosses the native boundary, should the Python facade remain reusable?
decision: When a Python fatal BaseException is propagated through the D431 host-boundary abort path, the Python facade must automatically poison/close its host-owned public objects after preserving propagation of the original fatal. Later facade use is rejected with an idiomatic closed/poisoned-facade error. This is host lifetime cleanup only: it must not emit protocol DATA, ERROR, COMPLETE, or TEARDOWN, must not create observe/topology semantics, and must not claim transactional rollback of already-committed graph effects.
rationale: D428 makes fatal BaseException values host-boundary failures that propagate to Python rather than graph ERROR or SubscriberCallbackError. D431 says post-fatal callers should discard or close the host graph facade; automatic poisoning makes that rule enforceable and prevents accidental reuse of possibly partially committed host/native state. D415 keeps this in Python lifetime policy while preserving the synchronous Rust engine and protocol semantics.

layer: L6 / Workspace proposal family outcome concrete API shape / D434 follow-up
question: What concrete API, default completion policy, horizon material, repair vocabulary, and outcome index shape should implement D434?
decision: Workspace family application outcomes use four family-owned pure record helpers for required-input response, WorkItem spawn, WorkItem link, and WorkItem domain action. Each helper consumes a generic WorkspaceProposalApplicationStatusRecord plus Workspace/family-supplied outcome id, sourceRefs, audit, and family-specific result refs, and returns recorded/not-recorded preview material with issues; no public generic family-outcome recorder is added. Default completion policy is data-only: required-input response requires one recorded outcome with requiredInputRequestId and responseRef, WorkItem spawn requires one recorded outcome with workItemRef, WorkItem link requires one recorded outcome with linkRef, and domain action requires one recorded outcome with actionRef unless an explicit policy enables multi-step partial completion. Evidence horizon is structured Workspace/family-owned material with sourceRefs/audit; generic projection cannot close it by query timeout. repair-needed lowers only to human-visible repair review/request material, never automatic remutation. Family outcome indexing is a pure projected thin-ref index over family facts keyed by application/idempotency coordinates, not storage and not full fact denormalization.
rationale: D434 locks family ownership and generic thinness but leaves concrete implementation shape open. This design gives each family a narrow owner API, keeps completion/horizon/indexing explainable as pure data projection, and gives repair-needed a visible path without creating a retry command bus or generic fact emitter.

layer: L6 / Workspace proposal family application prerequisite diagnostics / D430-D437 follow-up
question: When a Workspace proposal family application context references missing durable WorkspaceProposalRecorded or WorkspaceProposalAdmissionDecision material, may the family projector synthesize WorkspaceProposalApplicationStatus or application envelope material?
decision: Workspace proposal family application projectors must not synthesize WorkspaceProposalApplicationStatus, proposalId, decisionId, application envelope material, family facts, or family outcome material when the referenced durable WorkspaceProposalRecorded or WorkspaceProposalAdmissionDecision is missing. Missing durable proposal/admission prerequisites may emit context-scoped issue and audit diagnostics only, keyed to the application context and available refs, and then wait for durable material to arrive. Once both durable record and durable admission decision are present, normal D430/D434/D437 validation and application projection may run. Canvas, root exports, and workspace-intents remain preview/navigation surfaces and must not become proposal, admission, application, or diagnostic authority.
rationale: D430 requires durable admission before family application consumes it, while D434-D437 keep generic application status thin and family outcomes owned by family helpers. A family application context alone does not contain enough authority to construct the generic application status envelope without inventing proposal/admission identity or status. Diagnostic-only missing-prerequisite material preserves observability without creating a command bus, retry path, or synthetic application truth.

layer: L6 / Workspace proposal family diagnostic projection and repair-review handoff / D438 follow-up
question: How should Workspace proposal family diagnostics and repair-review requests be projected after D438 without turning diagnostics, Canvas, root exports, or workspace-intents into application or repair authority?
decision: Workspace proposal family diagnostics use a Workspace-owned projection over existing issue, audit, WorkspaceProposalApplicationStatus, WorkspaceProposalApplicationRecorded, family outcome status, and family outcome index material. The diagnostic projection is read-only and may produce human-visible diagnostic view material, but it must not create proposal, admission, application, family fact, family outcome, or canonical repair authority. Missing durable WorkspaceProposalRecorded or WorkspaceProposalAdmissionDecision diagnostics from D438 enter only the diagnostic view and cannot produce WorkspaceProposalApplicationStatus, repair-needed, repair review request, family outcome, or remutation. Repair review requests lower only from durable idempotency-conflict or missing-family-material/repair-needed status, outcome, or index material that already has durable proposal/admission/application coordinates. Malformed family material remains diagnostic-only unless a later decision widens repair-review eligibility. Repair review request material is human-visible, data-only, non-remutating, and does not authorize automatic retry, family fact creation, proposal/admission/application mutation, or runtime execution. Canvas, root exports, and workspace-intents remain preview/navigation surfaces and must not become diagnostic, repair, proposal, admission, or application authority.
rationale: D438 preserves observability for missing durable prerequisites without synthesizing application truth, while D434-D437 allow durable repair-needed and idempotency-conflict material to lower to human-visible review. This decision separates diagnostic visibility from repair authority, prevents missing-prerequisite or malformed-material issues from becoming retry paths, and keeps repair review anchored to durable Workspace status/outcome material rather than Canvas previews, workspace-intents, root exports, or generic issue streams.

layer: L6 / Canvas proposal family diagnostic display and outcome drilldown boundary / D437-D439 follow-up
question: How should Canvas display diagnostic-only proposal family application read-models, bridge read-model descriptors to UI, and support outcome drilldown without turning descriptors into commands or indexes into full fact stores?
decision: Canvas proposal family application display uses pure read-model and component descriptor data only. A diagnostic-only read-model is valid Canvas display material for D438/D439 diagnostic contexts, but it must not synthesize WorkspaceProposalApplicationStatus, proposal/admission/application envelope material, family handoff/completion/evidence/repair shells, family facts, repair review requests, or outcome refs. Renderer descriptor projection should distinguish malformed or non-data read-model input from valid diagnostic-only display material by emitting an explicit diagnostic display descriptor or diagnostic display mode, never by treating D438/D439 diagnostic-only material as a runtime error. Host React/runtime bridges may consume descriptors and map descriptor kinds to trusted host-owned components, but Canvas descriptors must not contain callbacks, commands, command intents, provider/runtime/client/credential handles, file/network operations, admission/application/diagnostic/repair owner APIs, or mutation material. Family outcome indexes remain thin ref indexes for replay/divergence visibility only; any Canvas drilldown over outcome facts must use a separate read-only detail projector that consumes explicit supplied facts plus thin refs, validates coordinates, supports bounded pagination/filtering, and never denormalizes full facts into the index or records/mutates domain truth.
rationale: D437 keeps family outcome indexes thin and repair display-only, D438 requires missing prerequisite contexts to remain diagnostic-only rather than synthetic application envelopes, and D439 separates Workspace diagnostic visibility from repair authority. Canvas still needs a first-class way to render diagnostic-only material and later inspect outcome details. Splitting diagnostic display descriptors from malformed input and splitting detail projection from the thin index preserves auditability, replay visibility, and UI usefulness without creating a command surface, runtime bridge, storage cursor, generic family fact reader, or Canvas-owned diagnostic/repair authority.

layer: L6 / Workspace proposal repair-review lifecycle / D439 follow-up
question: How should Workspace proposal repair-review requests gain current lifecycle visibility without mutating requests or authorizing automatic repair?
decision: WorkspaceProposalRepairReviewRequest remains immutable human-visible handoff material. Current repair-review lifecycle is projected by separate Workspace-owned status/view material over repair review requests, durable application/outcome/index material, and explicit human review decision material. Lifecycle states such as open, acknowledged, resolved, withdrawn, and superseded are read-model/status facts only; they do not delete requests, remutate proposals, create family facts, satisfy input gates, or execute runtimes. Resolution or supersession may be projected only from explicit durable successor material with matching proposal/admission/application/idempotency/family coordinates or from explicit human review decision material, never from absence of a diagnostic or repair-needed fact. Any actual repair action must enter through a new proposal/admission/application path with Workspace-supplied ids and policy.
rationale: D439 allows repair review requests as visible handoff but intentionally leaves lifecycle unresolved. Splitting immutable requests from current lifecycle view preserves replay/audit, prevents hidden autonomous repair, and lets UI hide stale requests only when durable or human-visible material proves their status.

layer: L6 / Workspace diagnostic projection pattern / D439-D440 follow-up
question: Should Workspace diagnostics become a generic public diagnostic primitive now, or remain domain-owned projections with only mechanical reuse?

Family application diagnostics keep their own classification, eligibility, coordinate validation, and repair-review lowering boundaries. Shared reuse may extract only internal mechanical helpers such as stable id construction, replay dedupe signatures, bounded metadata normalization, coordinate equality, and view ordering after repeated domains prove identical needs. No public root WorkspaceDiagnostic primitive, Canvas diagnostic authority, workspace-intents diagnostic bus, generic issue-to-repair lowerer, or root export is added in this slice. A future Workspace-wide diagnostic view may aggregate already-projected domain diagnostics but must not reinterpret raw issues or create proposal, admission, application, family truth, or repair authority.
rationale: D439 deliberately separates diagnostic visibility from application and repair authority, and D440 keeps Canvas display read-only. Premature generic diagnostics would turn issue/audit/status material into a broad authority surface before multiple domains prove stable shared semantics. Domain-owned projection preserves single-source classification while leaving safe room for mechanical helper reuse.

layer: L6 / Python advanced ctx authoring facade / CSP-7
question: Should Python Graph.node expose advanced node option flags as public keyword-only ctx-level authoring controls?
decision: Python may expose keyword-only advanced Graph.node options that map directly to Rust native NodeOpts for ctx-level authoring: partial, complete_when_deps_complete, error_when_deps_error, and terminal_as_real_input. These options are public advanced authoring surface, not raw protocol message APIs. They must not expose raw Node.up(msgs), arbitrary message construction/sending, or Python-only protocol aliases.

D77/D78/C-23 require raw ctx waveData and terminal metadata to be usable without inventing Python-only semantics. C-15/C-17 need terminal/gate behavior to be expressible through native NodeOpts. Keyword-only flags preserve host-natural Python ergonomics while avoiding raw message exposure forbidden by D435.

layer: L6 / Workspace proposal repair-review lifecycle concrete shape / D441 follow-up
question: What concrete TypeScript repair-review decision/status shape, precedence, and durable proof rules should implement D441?
decision: Workspace repair-review lifecycle uses separate WorkspaceProposalRepairReviewDecision and WorkspaceProposalRepairReviewStatus material. Repair review requests remain immutable handoff facts. Decisions carry reviewDecisionId, repairRequestId, full application/proposal/admission-decision/idempotency/family coordinates, reviewer or actor/audit/sourceRefs, lifecycle intent, reason/code, and optional resolves/supersedes refs. Status projection consumes repair review requests, review decisions, application statuses, application-recorded material, family outcome statuses, and family outcome index entries, and emits current lifecycle states such as open, acknowledged, resolved, withdrawn, superseded, or conflict. All lifecycle inputs must match the request coordinates; mismatched material is ignored or diagnostic-only. Precedence is explicit human terminal decision, then explicit durable resolved/superseded proof, then acknowledged, then open; acknowledged never overrides durable resolution. Conflicting incomparable human decisions fail closed as conflict rather than latest-wins. Durable resolved proof is limited to matching recorded family outcome status/index material with outcome refs, matching applied/recorded application status with emitted family refs, or WorkspaceProposalApplicationRecorded joined to a matching application status. Absence of diagnostics, absence of repair-needed material, malformed family material, Canvas display state, root exports, or workspace-intents never resolves or supersedes a repair review request.
rationale: D441 separates immutable handoff from current lifecycle but leaves concrete status, precedence, and proof rules open. A narrow explicit shape preserves replay/audit, prevents UI or absence-based lifecycle inference, and lets repair review close only when human-visible or durable Workspace material proves it.

layer: L6 / Canvas proposal family read-model composition handoff / D440-D444 follow-up
question: How should Canvas consume proposal family diagnostics, repair-review lifecycle, and outcome drilldown without reclassifying raw facts or becoming repair/application authority?
decision: Canvas consumes Workspace-owned proposal family application read-model and descriptor material, not raw issue/audit/status streams for its own classification. The read-model projector may compose family application diagnostics, repair-review lifecycle statuses, thin outcome indexes, and explicitly supplied outcome facts into bounded diagnostic, repair-review, and outcome-detail display records. It must validate coordinates, preserve thin refs, support bounded pagination/filtering for drilldown, and mark missing or mismatched detail material as display diagnostics. It must not synthesize application status, family facts, repair requests, repair decisions, proposal/admission/application ids, provider/runtime actions, callbacks, commands, or mutation intents. Canvas descriptors remain read-only display material and may only route user action through existing proposal/admission/application or review-decision paths owned by Workspace.

A Workspace-owned read-model handoff prevents Canvas from becoming a classifier or repair authority while still giving product UI a coherent bounded surface.

layer: L6 / Canvas proposal family host display, repair decision intake, and outcome detail supply boundary / D440-D445 follow-up
question: How should host React runtimes consume Canvas proposal family descriptors, how should repair-review human decisions be created and audited, and how should outcome detail facts be supplied without turning Canvas descriptors into commands or thin indexes into fact stores?

Outcome detail fact supply remains separate from the thin outcome index: any storage/query/runtime integration must be a read-only family/Workspace detail selector or host-supplied explicit fact source that validates requested thin refs and coordinates, returns bounded supplied facts or diagnostics for the existing detail projector, and never stores cursors in the index, denormalizes full facts into the index, records facts, creates canonical ids, mutates domain truth, or becomes a generic family fact reader.

The remaining integration risk is accidental promotion of display descriptors into commands, review buttons into mutation authority, or outcome indexes into storage readers. layer: L6 / Python private conformance harness boundary / CSP-7

layer: L6 / Canvas proposal family drilldown query descriptor / D445-D446 follow-up

Dynamic UI paging/filtering still needs a durable request shape. Making query descriptors graph-visible preserves replay, describe/debuggability, and bounded view identity while keeping Canvas read-only and preventing host callbacks, thin indexes, or raw issue streams from becoming stores or classifiers.

layer: L6 / Workspace proposal repair action descriptor and successor handoff / D441-D448 follow-up
question: How may UI repair-review actions lead to human review decisions or actual repair work without turning repair lifecycle status into mutation authority?

UI may consume read-only WorkspaceProposalRepairActionDescriptor-style affordance material derived from repair-review requests/statuses and optional Workspace policy, but those descriptors are display affordances only. Recording acknowledgement, withdrawal, supersession, or human resolution enters through the Workspace-owned repair-review decision intake locked by D444/D446. Any actual repair, retry, replacement, or follow-up work must enter the ordinary Workspace proposal/admission/application path with Workspace-supplied ids, policy, actor/capability/audit/sourceRefs to the repair material, and family-owned application/outcome handling. Durable successor material may later resolve or supersede the original repair review only through D444 proof rules. Descriptors may carry actionKind, enabled/disabled reason, coordinates, and source refs, but not executable commands, form callbacks, draft factories, hidden retry policy, or canonical successor ids.
rationale: D441 explicitly requires actual repair action to enter a new proposal/admission/application path, D444 prevents lifecycle status from remutating, and D445/D448 keep Canvas read-only. A descriptor-only handoff gives Canvas actionable UX while preserving Workspace ownership of review decisions and normal proposal intake for real repair work, preventing a command bus, hidden retry path, or Canvas/application authority from emerging through UI affordances.

layer: L6 / Workspace proposal repair-review decision intake concrete shape / D441-D446 follow-up
question: What concrete helper shape should record human repair-review decisions without letting Canvas descriptors, current UI state, or repair affordances become mutation authority?

It copies proposal/application/admission/idempotency/family coordinates from the request rather than accepting caller-supplied coordinate overrides, validates data-only refs/metadata/audit, and never generates canonical ids. Current WorkspaceProposalRepairReviewStatus may be supplied only as optional guard/preview context for stale-state detection; it is not the authority for coordinates or permission. Recording a decision never mutates the request, application status, family outcome facts, WorkItems, RequiredInput gates, links, proposal/admission/application truth, or runtime state. Resolved/withdrawn/superseded decisions are lifecycle material only; any actual repair or domain mutation must enter through a separate proposal/admission/application path.
rationale: D441-D444 define repair-review lifecycle projection and D446 keeps Canvas descriptors out of decision authority. A narrow Workspace-owned recording helper gives UI and human review flows a concrete durable decision path while preserving auditability, no-autonomous-repair, explicit ids, and replay-safe status projection.

layer: L6 / Canvas proposal family host display slot contract / D440-D446 follow-up
question: What concrete boundary should let host React/runtime code render Canvas proposal family application descriptors without making Canvas own a public registry, callbacks, renderer lifecycle, permissions, or mutation commands?

Canvas may expose proposal application descriptor bundles, diagnostic descriptors, outcome detail read-models, event envelopes, and preview/lowering material, and may later expose type-only host slot props for descriptor consumption. Those host components may display descriptors, request read-only drilldown pages, or route user affordances to existing Workspace-owned preview/intake/repair-decision paths, but descriptor data itself remains read-only and must not contain executable behavior or authority.
rationale: D423 keeps renderer runtime binding caller-owned, D440-D445 keep Canvas descriptor/read-model material data-only, and D446 separates host rendering from repair decision intake and outcome fact supply. A host-owned display slot convention gives React/product code freedom to render trusted components while preventing Canvas from freezing a registry API or smuggling callbacks, commands, permissions, runtime handles, or mutation authority into descriptor DTOs.

layer: L6 / Workspace proposal family outcome detail fact supply boundary / D440-D446 follow-up
question: How should outcome detail facts be supplied for Canvas drilldown without turning thin outcome indexes into storage cursors, fact stores, or generic family fact readers?

A supply request/result may carry complete application/proposal/admission-decision/idempotency/workspace/family coordinates, requested thin outcome refs, bounded page/filter options, source refs, supplied outcome facts, missing refs, and diagnostics. The supply boundary may validate and filter explicit supplied facts for the requested refs, but it must not record facts, create canonical ids, mutate WorkItems/domain/application/family truth, call storage/query/runtime/provider/file/network APIs, or denormalize full facts into the thin outcome index. Any future storage/query/runtime integration must live outside the index as a separately reviewed read-only adapter or projector that emits explicit supplied facts or bounded supply results for the existing detail projector.
rationale: D437 and D440 keep family outcome indexes thin, while D445 and D446 require useful drilldown over explicit supplied facts without making Canvas or indexes authoritative. A separate supply boundary preserves pagination/filtering and host/storage integration room while keeping display projection, fact selection, and durable recording distinct.

layer: L6 / Workspace repair action intake handoff / D449-D450 follow-up
question: How should UI repair action descriptor selections enter Workspace-owned review decision or successor proposal intake without turning descriptors into commands or draft factories?
decision: UI selections of WorkspaceProposalRepairActionDescriptor material are represented as data-only repair action intent/intake material carrying descriptor/action identity, full repair coordinates, actor/reviewer/source/audit refs, and optional bounded metadata. Review-only actions lower only through the Workspace-owned repair-review decision recording path locked by D450, with reviewDecisionId, policy, audit, and sourceRefs supplied by Workspace/caller. Successor or follow-up actions enter a separate Workspace-owned successor proposal intake/preview path that may read the referenced repair request/status/material and policy to prepare proposal-ready material, but it must not itself record proposal/admission/application truth, generate canonical successor ids inside the descriptor, execute runtime/provider actions, or mutate family/application facts. Actual repair, retry, replacement, or follow-up work remains ordinary Workspace proposal/admission/application flow.
rationale: D449 makes repair action descriptors display affordances only, and D450 locks human repair-review decision recording. The remaining UI handoff needs a concrete intake boundary so buttons can be useful without becoming command buses, hidden draft factories, or repair authority. Splitting review-decision intake from successor proposal intake preserves auditability, explicit ids, Workspace policy ownership, and the normal proposal/admission/application path for real work.

layer: L6 / Python public PULL and pause-mode facade / CSP-7
question: How should Python expose public PULL and pause-mode ergonomics without violating D435/D443/D447 raw protocol boundaries?
decision: Python may extend public Graph.node keyword-only advanced options with pausable: bool | 'resumeAll' = True and pull_id: str | None = None, mapping directly to Rust native NodeOpts. Python may expose read-only Ctx.pull / PullContext and Ctx.pull_params() for holder-visible PULL demand context. Python may expose narrow Ctx.request_pull(...) and Ctx.request_pull_next(...) helpers that construct only PULL demand over declared dep edges, with optional toward_dep, and no arbitrary Message construction or raw ctx.up/Node.up surface. request_pull_next is the public self-demand path for D37-safe boundary-deferred PULL. pull_id + pausable=False must be rejected. Full public ctx.rewire_next topology mutation remains out of scope and requires a separate design decision.
rationale: R-pull/R-up-routing/R-ctx-up already define explicit PULL semantics, params, routing, and boundary-deferred self-demand. D415 gives Python an idiomatic facade over Rust native behavior, while D435 forbids raw Node.up/message sending and D447 requires separate design before public PULL/pause ergonomics. Narrow Python methods complete C-16/C-26/C-27 authoring without opening protocol escape hatches or Python-only aliases.

layer: L6 / Canvas proposal family read-model query extension discipline / D448-D453 follow-up
question: How may Canvas proposal family read-model drilldown add sort, group, and search controls without turning query descriptors into storage cursors, generic fact readers, classifiers, or mutation authority?

Sort/group/search fields must be closed, normalized, data-only, and included in read-model identity and dedupe signatures. These options must not introduce storage cursors, opaque continuation tokens, storage/query/runtime/provider calls, generic family fact reader semantics, raw issue classification, family fact synthesis, application status synthesis, repair/retry commands, proposal/admission/application id generation, callbacks, mutation intents, or Canvas-owned authority. rationale: D448 gives Canvas a graph-visible read-only query descriptor for bounded drilldown, while D445-D446 and D452 keep detail fact supply, thin indexes, and host/runtime integration separate from Canvas authority. Sort/group/search are useful display controls but can easily become hidden retrieval or classification surfaces. Keeping them closed, normalized, display-only, and identity-bearing preserves replay/debuggability and current-view semantics without promoting the query descriptor into a fact store, storage cursor, or command surface.

layer: L6 / Workspace proposal repair-review decision recording projector / D450-D453 follow-up
question: How should repair-review decision recording become graph-visible without making Canvas descriptors, current status, or repair action selections mutation authority?
decision: Workspace may add a graph-visible repair-review decision recording projector that consumes existing WorkspaceProposalRepairReviewRequest facts, explicit Workspace/caller-supplied WorkspaceProposalRepairReviewDecisionRecordingInput facts, and optional matching WorkspaceProposalRepairReviewStatus stale-guard material. rationale: D450 locks the pure decision-recording helper and D444 locks repair-review lifecycle projection. A graph-visible projector makes human review decisions replayable, inspectable, and composable while preserving Workspace ownership, explicit ids, auditability, stale-state guarding, and no-autonomous-repair.

layer: L6 / Workspace proposal outcome detail read-only selector adapter boundary / D452-D455 follow-up
question: How may real outcome detail facts be selected for drilldown without turning the thin outcome index or Canvas supply helper into storage readers?
decision: Real outcome detail selection must live outside the thin outcome index and outside the pure D452 supply helper as a separately reviewed read-only Workspace/family-owned selector adapter. The adapter may privately call storage/query/provider infrastructure, but graph-visible material may contain only bounded data-only supplied outcome facts or WorkspaceProposalFamilyApplicationOutcomeDetailFactSupplyResult-style DTOs. The adapter validates requested thin refs and coordinates, preserves missing/divergent/mismatched refs as diagnostics, and must not store cursors or full facts in the index, expose storage/query/provider/runtime/client/file/network handles in DATA, create ids, record facts, mutate truth, or become a generic family fact reader.
rationale: D452 keeps supply separate from thin indexes and D445 requires useful drilldown over explicit supplied facts. A separate selector-adapter boundary allows real data integration while keeping fact selection, display projection, thin indexing, and durable recording distinct.

layer: L6 / Canvas proposal descriptor host-owned rendering convention / D451 follow-up
question: Where should descriptorKind-to-component mapping live for proposal family application display?
decision: DescriptorKind-to-component mapping for proposal family application display is host-owned and runtime-private. Canvas may expose only data-only descriptor, read-model, and host-slot DTOs through focused surfaces. Hosts may privately map descriptor kinds to trusted UI components and route user affordances to existing Workspace-owned preview, intake, and repair-decision paths. Canvas must not expose a public component registry, React map, callback/action handler surface, renderer lifecycle, permission enforcement object, provider/runtime/client/credential/file/network handle, or mutation command API.

layer: L6 / Workspace repair action intent concrete shape / D449-D453 follow-up
question: What concrete data shape should represent UI repair action descriptor selections before they lower into Workspace-owned review decision or successor proposal intake?
decision: Workspace repair action selections use explicit data-only WorkspaceProposalRepairActionIntent-style material that carries an intent id, descriptor id, repairRequestId, actionKind, full application/proposal/admission-decision/idempotency/family coordinates, actor or reviewer refs, sourceRefs, optional audit, and optional bounded metadata. The intent itself must not carry commands, callbacks, draft factories, canonical successor proposal/admission/application ids, runtime/provider actions, family facts, application status, or mutation intents.

layer: L6 / Workspace repair successor proposal intake preview / D449-D453 follow-up
question: How should open-successor-proposal-flow prepare follow-up proposal context without becoming a hidden draft factory or generating canonical proposal/admission/application ids?

The preview consumes matching repair-review request/status material, repair action intent material, optional Workspace policy/context, and sourceRefs to produce bounded proposal-ready context such as suggested family, target refs, context refs, reason/code, display diagnostics, and optional data-only suggested draft patch material. Durable successor material may later resolve or supersede the original repair review only through D444 proof rules.

Successor flow is the highest-risk affordance because prefill can become a hidden draft factory. A preview-only shape preserves useful UI context while keeping canonical ids, policy, final draft, admission, application, and durable repair proof in Workspace-owned paths.

layer: L6 / Canvas proposal family read-model query concrete presentation options / D455 follow-up
question: What exact sort, group, and search option shape should D455 allow on proposal family read-model query descriptors?
decision: Concrete D455 query options use closed, data-only presentation fields. Group fields are limited to display groupings such as outcome-kind, repair-state, and diagnostic-code. Search is bounded text matching over explicitly supplied or already-projected display material, with closed fields such as outcome-id, outcome-kind, diagnostic-code, diagnostic-message, and repair-state. Query normalization must trim and bound search text, sort and dedupe repeated fields deterministically, validate closed fields, and include normalized sort/group/search together with page/filter/view identity in readModelId and dedupe signatures. Unknown or malformed presentation options fail closed as display diagnostics or empty bounded read-model material. Grouping may add display grouping material but must preserve flat read-model material and must not create family facts, classify raw issues, synthesize statuses, introduce storage cursors, or call storage/query/runtime/provider APIs.
rationale: D455 permits presentation-level sort/group/search but intentionally leaves exact fields open. Locking a small closed set gives implementation and tests stable normalization, identity, and fail-closed behavior while keeping search a bounded display match rather than a retrieval adapter or generic fact reader. Preserving flat read-model material keeps the existing D448/D445 handoff stable while allowing UI grouping as additive display material.

layer: L6 / Workspace proposal family outcome detail supply concrete shape / D452-D457 follow-up
question: What concrete request/result shape should supply outcome detail facts for proposal family drilldown before the read-model projector consumes them?
