layer: L6 / Python C-1 bridge child adapter attachment and deterministic diamond harness shape
question: How should Python complete C-1 bridge protobuf, ack-timeout, release ownership, and the future full C-1 diamond harness without exposing raw protocol/native handles or adding hidden schedulers?
decision: Python C-1 child adapters are native-owned declared topology attachments under the opaque Python WireBridge facade. wire_bridge_protobuf decodes inbound bytes through native canonical protobuf validation, projects graph-visible protobuf status/issues independently, and privately attaches the decoded semantic envelope or invalid ingress node as a bridge inbound source; public Python exposes only inbound_bytes, outbound_bytes, status, issues, and release. wire_bridge_ack_driver consumes a graph-visible monotonic clock and bridge pending-attempt facts, derives public WireBridgeAckTimeout facts for inspection, and privately attaches a command projection to the bridge ack-timeout command ingress; public Python must not expose WireBridgeCommand, command sources, imperative ack methods, timers, sleeps, missed/catch-up policy, or raw PyO3 handles. Python bridge child bundles are graph-lifetime-owned native resources: child release detaches only that child's inbound or command source and releases its owned topology; bridge release cascades still-live children in reverse attachment order before releasing bridge-owned resources; Graph.close releases registered C-1 bundles in reverse creation order. Native detach happens before topology release and failed release restores the detached attachment when possible; release is idempotent lifecycle cleanup only and emits no protocol terminal. The eventual full C-1 mixed-locality diamond conformance harness uses two real graph domains connected by explicit deterministic host transport pump steps over canonical protobuf bytes; the pump is test/host transport, not a hidden core scheduler or retry timer, and must not shortcut through in-process shared graph wiring. C-1 remains todo until that full bridge diamond proves single-wave dirty/data coalescing end-to-end; C-1a/C-1b/C-1c may pass only when the focused Python public/native behavior is honestly covered by tests.
rationale: D516 and D521 require Python C-1 to stay high-level, bytes-only, graph-visible, and native-owned without raw protocol or PyO3 handle leakage. D523 requires protobuf transport to be a bytes facade with malformed material becoming status/issues rather than local protocol terminals. D524 requires ack timeouts to enter through explicit graph-visible facts while keeping retry ownership inside the bridge and forbidding hidden timer pumps. D527 requires graph-lifetime release, child-only release, bridge cascade, reverse Graph.close cleanup, and detach-before-release rollback. D529 keeps C-1a/C-1b/C-1c focused and prevents them from overclaiming the full mixed-locality C-1 diamond. Locking the attachment and harness shape now lets the implementation finish Python behavior by extending the existing TS/Rust declared-source patterns instead of inventing Python-only ingress, raw command surfaces, imperative callbacks, or scheduler shortcuts.

layer: L6 / Python graph-owned activation root

The shared abstraction is therefore a graph-owned activation release token, not an observer Subscription. A dedicated Python Retain handle preserves that cross-runtime shape while remaining Python-idiomatic through release() and context-manager support. It rejects undefined, NaN, infinities, -0, subnormal numbers, unsafe integers, bigint, symbols, functions, accessors/getters/setters, class instances, non-plain prototypes, Date/Map/Set/Error/Promise/thenables, sparse arrays, non-index array properties, symbol keys, cycles, Node/Ctx handles, live topology, mutable graph-owned state, raw command sources, host runtime objects, and local pending/diamond accounting. Python bytearray-like material may cross only by copying to immutable bytes; no live mutable buffer may be retained. Remote-call orphan response visibility is explicit: valid terminal responses with matching requestId plus operation correlation consume pending and emit result/error; valid status responses with matching correlation remain non-terminal and do not consume pending; operation mismatch, unknown/early/stale/duplicate-after-completion, and orphan responses emit issue/status material and do not consume pending; malformed responses with matching requestId and operation emit issue plus call-level error and consume pending to avoid immortal requests; malformed responses without current correlation emit issue only. TS ack-driver uses the focused D502 `wireBridgeAckDriver(graph, bridge, {clock, timeoutMs, name?})` shape, not a hidden timer and not a generic scheduled-readiness public burden: it exposes timeout, status, issue, and release material; privately projects due timeouts into bridge-owned ack-timeout command ingress; invalid/regressing clocks emit issues and no timeout; release detaches the private command source, releases owned retains/topology, and remains idempotent with no protocol terminal. The Python C-1 mixed-locality replay probe is decode-only diagnostic material around the deterministic FIFO byte pump, with trace rows carrying phase, direction, pump_step, queue_index, bytes_len, session_id, seq, cursor, attempt, envelope_type, payload_kind, data_body_kind, edge_id, cause_id, wire_edge_kind, value_hex_prefix, and decode_error. The probe must classify old-cause replay source without filtering, deduping, shortcutting, or repairing transport: old value in outbound before pump indicates outbound cause generation; valid old cause accepted and released inbound indicates WireEdgeGroup gate; warmup frames observed after clearing runs indicate activation/drain boundary. C-1 remains todo until the full mixed-locality diamond passes end to end.
rationale: D558 locked the boundary discipline, but B98 still needed exact implementation choices so each runtime does not choose a different whitelist, orphan-response outlet, ack-driver API, or replay-probe semantics. The strict JSON/bytes whitelist reuses existing canonical JSON and protobuf precedents while preventing raw host/runtime/topology state from crossing. The orphan-response contract sharpens D147/D155 without introducing future-response buffers. The TS ack-driver clause follows D502/D424 while keeping C-1c helper ergonomics focused. The probe trace lets the next slice locate the duplicate old-cause DATA source without turning the host pump into a semantic filter. This preserves D496/D500/D542, focused C-1a/C-1b/C-1c honesty under D529, R-no-raw-async, R-no-imperative, F-SYNC-CORE, F-DISPATCH-ALL, and no protocol/tier/message/ctx/verb changes.

layer: L6 / B98-C1 WireEdgeGroup outbound cause formation
question: How does outbound WireEdgeGroup form a new wire cause without reusing stale snapshots in mixed-locality diamonds?
decision: Outbound WireEdgeGroup emits a new wire-edge cause only from a fresh full-edge cohort: every expected outbound edge must provide DATA since the previous emitted cause before any DIRTY/DATA frames for the new cause are emitted. Retained snapshots may support status/diagnostics but must not fill missing edges in a new cause. Partial cohorts are graph-visible nonterminal issue/status material and remain local to the adapter; they do not emit protocol terminals and do not require host pump filtering, dedupe, repair, timers, schedulers, or protocol changes. If an edge updates multiple times before the cohort completes, the latest fresh DATA for that edge wins. On cohort completion, the adapter emits DIRTY for all expected edges, then DATA for all expected edges, using only pending fresh cohort material, and clears the pending cohort for the next cause. On SENTINEL or invalidation for an edge, the adapter clears that edge's pending fresh material and retained snapshot/status as appropriate and emits no wire cause.
rationale: This preserves D496 static WireEdgeGroup v1 and D558/D559 host pump discipline while preventing mixed-locality diamonds from turning stale retained snapshots into new outbound causes. It keeps cause correctness inside the WireEdgeGroup adapter boundary, leaves retained snapshots as diagnostics/status material only, and maintains D529 honesty that C-1a/C-1b/C-1c prerequisites do not by themselves satisfy the full C-1 mixed-locality diamond.

layer: L6 / B98-C1 WireEdgeGroup outbound fresh-source admission
question: How should outbound WireEdgeGroup distinguish fresh edge DATA from activation/current replay without payload dedupe or protocol lineage?
decision: Outbound WireEdgeGroup fresh-cohort admission is event-origin based. A group may admit one initial lifecycle bootstrap cohort from the first complete set of edge DATA, but after a cause has been emitted, a new cause may be formed only from dependency DATA occurrences produced by fresh graph events since the previous emitted cause. Activation/current snapshot replay, late-subscriber drain, retained values, and status/diagnostic replay must not by themselves admit a new outbound cause. Freshness must not be decided by payload equality: a fresh occurrence that produces the same bytes as a prior value is still eligible cohort material. Inbound WireEdgeGroup remains a structural cause lifecycle gate only and must not perform stale-payload dedupe. Host pumps remain deterministic FIFO byte transport with no filtering, dedupe, repair, timers, schedulers, or protocol changes.
rationale: This completes D560's fresh-cohort rule at the outbound admission boundary while preserving D496 static WireEdgeGroup v1, D558/D559 host-pump discipline, D529 honesty that C-1 remains todo until the full mixed-locality diamond passes, and R-resolved-undirty's rule that occurrence is not value equality. The bootstrap carve-out preserves legal initial activation/warmup, while the post-emission gate prevents current-value replay from creating new wire causes such as the observed return-leg new-cause/stale-payload sequence.

layer: L6 / B101 inbound WireEdgeGroup adapter-projector drain before tombstone/reset
question: How should B101 strengthen inbound WireEdgeGroup release timing after the B98/C-1 closeout without changing protocol semantics or host pump responsibility?
decision: Inbound WireEdgeGroup should strengthen the post-B98 release timing from release-cohort admission/enqueue-before-tombstone to adapter-projector drain-before-tombstone/reset. On a complete inbound cause, the adapter must publish one private release cohort containing all expected edge values and must not mark that cause released, add its released-cause tombstone, or reset active cause state until the adapter-owned inbound edge projectors have consumed that release cohort. The drain scope is exactly the WireEdgeGroup private release lane and its owned inbound edge projector nodes; it is not arbitrary downstream graph drain. Application downstream nodes, external subscribers, pause/resumeAll replay, batch commit/rollback beyond the adapter-owned release lane, queued boundary tasks, downstream throwing subscribers, and cross-graph consequences are outside this adapter-local guarantee. Implementations may use private graph-visible adapter topology/state such as an ack/tombstone lane or finalizer, but must keep public API unchanged. Full graph downstream drain remains a protocol/runtime semantic and requires spec-amend first: rules, formal model, and conformance before code. Host pumps remain deterministic FIFO byte transport only and must not become ACK, filtering, dedupe, repair, timer, scheduler, or drain participants. Payload equality stale dedupe, WireEdgeFrame parent/epoch/lineage, protocol tier/message/verb/ctx expansion, raw command/native handles, Node.up/down, and ctx.up/down exposure remain forbidden.
rationale: B98 and C-1 close out under the accepted WireEdgeGroup release-lane isolation evidence, but the prior timing was only successful release-cohort admission/enqueue before tombstone/reset and must not be overclaimed as downstream drain. B101 chooses the narrow stronger guarantee that remains inside the adapter boundary: private inbound edge projectors must consume the coherent release cohort before the cause becomes recently released and local active state is cleared. This preserves D558/D559 host-pump discipline, D560/D561 freshness rules, D506 bounded tombstone discipline, D22 graph-domain boundaries, F-SYNC-CORE, and F-NO-IMPL-DEFINED while giving the next implementation slice a precise target. A full graph drain barrier would cross into wave/batch/pause/error semantics and therefore belongs to spec-amend, not a WireEdgeGroup-only decision.

layer: L6 / public website and docs migration architecture
question: How should GraphReFly migrate public website and documentation ownership after clean-slate without exposing internal control docs as the product docs, reviving stale TypeScript website authority, or duplicating language API docs?
decision: The graphrefly repo owns the shared public website shell and public documentation architecture for graphrefly.dev, but graphrefly.dev is a curated external developer documentation site, not the full internal authority dashboard. Public website pages should render user-facing views from selected structured authority records and docs records: learn/getting-started, core concepts, composition patterns, examples, language package entry points, and a curated reference/guarantees layer. Internal/maintainer authority views, including full decisions, full rules, backlog, sessions, gaps, conformance coverage, dashboard search, and project control state, remain in the generated dashboard and raw repo records; they may be linked for maintainers but must not become the primary public docs experience. New shared docs content should default to structured JSONL records with stable ids, audience/publicness metadata, source refs, and links to governing rules/decisions/conformance where applicable. guide/guide.jsonl is the guide registry; composition, testing, contribute, and similar guide families should be represented as guide-local JSONL record sets rather than new long-form markdown as the default. Markdown prose such as GRAPHREFLY-SPEC.md and COMPOSITION-GUIDE*.md is migration/reference material until clean content is extracted into structured records, then it should be archived or removed; it is not canonical and must not be copied wholesale into graphrefly.dev. The old graphrefly-ts website is visual/tooling reference only, not protocol/docs authority. TypeScript, Python, and Rust repos keep ownership of generated API references, examples, demos, package-local release/install docs, and package-local docs generation; graphrefly.dev may link, delegate, or embed admitted package docs routes but must not hand-maintain mirrors. Public graphrefly.dev reference pages may expose curated active protocol guarantees and selected rule-derived views, but the full raw spec/decision/control surface belongs to dashboard/repo authority views. Any future change that makes graphrefly.dev the canonical home for package APIs, package demos, package releases, generated language references, deploy ownership for language-local docs, or a full public mirror of internal dashboard state requires a new decision before implementation.
rationale: The migration needs a single ownership boundary before more website work lands. D32 keeps language packages self-contained, D24 defines cross-language parity as behavioral conformance rather than symbol/document parity, D41 rejects old root/pure-ts authority revival, and the single-source-of-truth value forbids hand-maintained public mirrors. A public docs site must teach ordinary developers what to use and why, while the dashboard remains the searchable authority/control surface for maintainers and implementers. Structured JSONL records preserve source-of-truth discipline and let the website render different audience views without duplicating spec, guide, or decision text. This decision locks the migration direction while leaving deploy mechanics, route implementation, and record schemas to B6/B7 follow-up slices.

layer: L6 / Canvas graph-first topology lens and WorkGraph construction boundary / D390 correction
question: How should Canvas source Topology Lens topology and build its own Workbench product slices without creating a parallel Canvas topology that drifts from real GraphReFly graph structure?
decision: Canvas Topology Lens primary topology truth is the live @graphrefly/ts graph inspection surface: graph.topology(), graph.describe(), boundary inspection, or a host-admitted DescribeSnapshot/GraphTopologySnapshot derived from those surfaces. Canvas feature logic should prefer named @graphrefly/ts graph bundles and graph-visible projection facts for nontrivial Workbench behavior so the lens can reveal the real construction graph rather than a hand-built parallel topology. The D390 WorkspaceGraph topology projection is superseded as the default lens source: deriveWorkspaceTopology and WorkspaceTopologyModel may remain as product semantic overlays, compatibility/fallback material for host-admitted data records, or annotations over real graph nodes/edges, but they must not be treated as the primary topology truth when a real graph snapshot is available. WorkItem, WorkGraphRef, widget, review, evidence, and host-feedback product records remain data/ref material under D537-D539/D555; they do not become live substrate handles, hydrate authority, provider/storage cursors, executor permission, WorkItem mutation authority, or graph truth mutation routes. Canvas may adapt real graph nodes/edges into renderer-friendly lens display rows and may attach product overlays such as pinned widget state, selected scope, stale/evidence/status summaries, and typed follow-up affordances, but overlays must preserve provenance and must not invent substrate edges, hide topology changes behind imperative side channels, or overwrite graph.describe()/topology() truth. Session-local lens UI state remains governed by D507. If a host supplies only data records and no admitted graph snapshot, Canvas must label the rendered topology as product/semantic fallback rather than real graph topology. Future Canvas implementation slices that add durable WorkGraph, topology, scope, or control-panel surfaces must state whether the source is real graph inspection, product overlay, or fallback semantic projection, and dev-dispatch must route any new generic graph-inspection API, protocol/topology behavior, or @graphrefly/ts surface change through design review before implementation.
rationale: D240 and D345 intended WorkspaceGraph and Canvas to sit over ordinary GraphReFly topology and graph-visible facts, but D390 allowed a pure Canvas product selector to become the practical Topology Lens path. That was safe against substrate-authority leakage but wrong for the Workbench product promise: if Canvas itself is graph-backed work, the reviewer should see the real graph grow as features are built, not a second DTO topology maintained beside it. @graphrefly/ts already owns topology()/describe()/boundary inspection, and graphrefly-ts README/implementation position those as read-only inspection surfaces over live topology truth. Superseding D390 as the primary lens source avoids future workaround layers, preserves graph-first inspectability, keeps Canvas product overlays bounded, and still honors D537-D539/D555 by preventing product refs or widgets from becoming runtime handles or mutation authority.

layer: L6 / Canvas graph-built implementation and dev-dispatch topology delta reporting / D564 follow-up
question: How should Canvas code itself use @graphrefly/ts so dev-dispatch can report real node/edge progress instead of prose-only implementation status?
decision: Canvas implementation should default to named @graphrefly/ts graph bundles for nontrivial Workbench/product behavior whose state, dependency, execution-visibility, or review shape is graph-like. Durable graph-built slices should expose stable graph names, topologyGroup names, node names, and testable graph.topology()/graph.describe() snapshots or fixture snapshots so implementation progress can be reviewed as real added, removed, or changed nodes and edges. dev-dispatch implementation rounds that touch graph-built Canvas surfaces must report a real topology delta when a before/after graph inspection source is available: added nodes, removed nodes, changed node factories/deps/meta/status-source, added edges, removed edges, and any product overlay deltas separately labeled as overlays. If a slice is docs-only, pure type/DTO/schema, static copy, CSS/layout, React rendering without graph behavior, or fallback semantic projection work, dev-dispatch must say no real graph delta is available and why; repeated no-delta product slices are a roadmap health smell after D564. This does not require forcing every type, static DTO, React component, visual style, fixture, or boundary display record into a graph node. Canvas must not push Canvas-owned symbols into @graphrefly/ts, create Graph subclasses, use graph nodes as provider/storage/credential/runtime handles, mutate WorkItems or graph truth through UI, or invent hand-authored node delta reports. Graph delta reports must be derived from @graphrefly/ts inspection or tests that construct the real bundle, while semantic overlays remain separate display material. Future slices that add or modify graph-built Canvas bundles should include acceptance evidence for topology snapshot stability and node naming sufficient for user review.
rationale: D564 corrected the Topology Lens source but does not by itself force Canvas implementation work to be inspectable as graph construction progress. The user's review loop depends on seeing the real graph grow: if Canvas product behavior is graph-like but implemented as detached DTO logic, dev-dispatch can only summarize prose and cannot honestly report changed nodes. Requiring graph-built bundles where appropriate preserves GraphReFly dogfooding, makes topology deltas reviewable, and prevents future workaround layers, while the exemptions keep Canvas from turning plain UI, DTO boundaries, or static display material into fake graph truth. This extends D240/D345/D537-D539/D555/D564 without changing protocol or @graphrefly/ts ownership.

layer: L6 / Rust CSP-10 baseline application-infrastructure scope
question: In Rust CSP-10, which retained TypeScript application-infrastructure surfaces belong in the baseline graphrefly-rs product surface, and which should remain deferred as higher application/vertical layers?
decision: Rust CSP-10 baseline includes reusable graph-visible application-infrastructure primitives such as messaging, generic orchestration/readiness, work queue, CQRS/process recipes, and related status/audit/cursor/readiness/projector vocabulary when they are Rust-relevant and can be expressed as ordinary graph facts, declared deps, passive policy/data vocabulary, or graph-visible bundles. These belong below patterns/solutions and may be used by them. Rust should not defer messaging/orchestration/work_queue merely because they are above the substrate; they are part of the basic reusable GraphReFly infrastructure surface. Deferred higher-layer scope remains LLM/vector/provider runtime adapters, product-specific WorkItem/Canvas/agent semantics, ontology policy, alias/provenance repair, multi-writer conflict repair, provider-specific context adapters, and vertical solution runtimes unless a separate design review locks a narrow Rust-native shape.
rationale: B63/D125 classify messaging, orchestration, and CQRS as reusable application infrastructure rather than patterns or vertical solutions. D130-D132 lock graph-visible environment/messaging/resilience adapter shapes; D424/D432/D433 lock scheduled readiness as provider/domain-neutral orchestration; B94/B95 show workQueue readiness convergence as generic infrastructure; B67/B72/B74 already record Rust-native intent coverage for messaging, workQueue, scheduled readiness, process/CQRS recipes, and related examples. Locking this boundary prevents two opposite drifts: under-scoping Rust by excluding reusable app-infra as too application-layer, or over-scoping Rust by pulling in LLM/vector/provider/agent product layers before concrete design. No protocol, tier, message, ctx, batch, storage-restore, or cross-language conformance behavior changes.

layer: L6 / Rust EnvironmentDrivers streaming runtime boundary / B72
question: Should Rust B72 close deferred runtime-driver design with a broad RuntimeDriver abstraction or a narrower generic HTTP byte-stream capability?
decision: Rust should add a narrow graph-owned EnvironmentDrivers HTTP byte-stream capability, not a broad RuntimeDriver abstraction. The public shape is LocalHttpStreamDriver over HttpRequest to HttpStreamDriverEvent { Head, Chunk, Error, Complete }, installed through EnvironmentDrivers and implemented by optional concrete drivers such as TokioHttpStreamDriver. Typed source adapters such as from_sse may use this capability to parse protocol-specific events, while preserving existing typed LocalSseDriver compatibility as needed. The stream capability is inbound/network-only boundary work: it does not execute providers, own schedulers, mutate graph truth, expose runtime handles, create generic sinks, replace WebSocket session semantics, or merge with Dispatcher WorkerPool or wire-bridge responsibilities. All async work remains outside the sync wave core and re-enters through existing source/DeferredCtx paths. No protocol, tier, message, ctx, batch, conformance, readiness, workQueue, CQRS, or provider-runtime semantics change.
rationale: D130-D132 allow EnvironmentDrivers to grow concrete process/network/runtime drivers when product needs require them, but reject broad generic sink surfaces and require typed graph-visible facts/bundles. D137 separates EnvironmentDrivers task/runtime work from Dispatcher WorkerPool and wire bridge work. A narrow HTTP byte-stream driver closes the real Rust gap behind from_sse and future inbound streaming adapters without freezing a monolithic RuntimeDriver contract or making raw streaming a new graph authority. Keeping response head/chunk/error/complete as driver-boundary events preserves inspectable typed source nodes, testable cancellation, optional dependency footprint, and F-SYNC-CORE.

layer: L6 / Rust SSE source over HTTP stream / B72-D567
question: How should Rust from_sse use the new D567 HTTP byte-stream capability without leaving competing SSE driver authorities or creating a broad streaming API?
decision: Rust from_sse/from_sse_with_options should resolve SSE input through a typed override plus stream fallback. If EnvironmentDrivers contains a LocalSseDriver, from_sse uses that protocol-specific driver exactly as today. If no LocalSseDriver is installed but a LocalHttpStreamDriver is present, from_sse lowers SseRequest to an HTTP GET stream request, adds Accept: text/event-stream when absent, validates the response head, parses chunks into SseEvent values inside the source adapter, and emits DATA/ERROR/COMPLETE through the existing DeferredCtx source path. Official Rust concrete runtime support should implement TokioHttpStreamDriver rather than a separate TokioSseDriver. LocalSseDriver remains a typed override/test/host-parsed protocol hook, not the default concrete runtime-driver direction. The SSE parser is adapter-local implementation, not a public generic stream parser, not a provider/runtime adapter, not a retry/reconnect scheduler, and not a replacement for WebSocket session semantics. No protocol, tier, message, ctx, batch, conformance, readiness, workQueue, CQRS, or provider-runtime semantics change.
rationale: D567 locks the generic inbound HTTP byte-stream capability while preserving typed source adapters. Keeping LocalSseDriver as the first-choice explicit override avoids breaking existing host-parsed/test drivers and respects user-installed protocol-specific capability. Falling back to LocalHttpStreamDriver gives Rust a concrete runtime path for from_sse without adding TokioSseDriver or broad RuntimeDriver surface. Adapter-local parsing preserves from_sse describe/topology shape, keeps async work at the EnvironmentDrivers boundary, and prevents raw byte streams from becoming graph truth or public application semantics.

layer: L6 / Rust HTTP stream driver event lifecycle / B72-D567-D568
question: What lifecycle contract should LocalHttpStreamDriver and TokioHttpStreamDriver follow so streaming network input remains deterministic boundary material rather than driver-defined runtime semantics?
decision: LocalHttpStreamDriver stream callbacks follow a strict finite transport lifecycle: each stream invocation emits either exactly one Head event followed by zero or more Chunk events and then exactly one terminal Complete or Error event, or emits exactly one Error event before any Head when setup/request/head acquisition fails. No Chunk may precede Head, no second Head may occur, and no callback may fire after driver-delivered terminal completion or after cancel has taken effect. Driver callbacks may occur synchronously before the DriverCancel is returned, so source adapters must fence active/terminal state independently of cancel-slot installation. HTTP status, headers, redirects, TLS, transport errors, and response-body errors remain driver boundary material; typed adapters decide whether a Head is semantically acceptable for their protocol. If an adapter rejects a Head, it emits adapter ERROR facts, marks itself inactive/terminal, ignores later driver chunks, and invokes the returned cancel once available. Empty byte chunks should be skipped by drivers when possible and ignored by typed adapters when observed. The driver owns no retry, reconnect, scheduler, buffering policy beyond transport iteration, parser state, backpressure authority, domain truth, or graph mutation authority. TokioHttpStreamDriver may use reqwest streaming under a feature gate, but dependency/runtime details do not enter public graph facts beyond Head/Chunk/Error/Complete.
rationale: D567 adds a narrow HTTP byte-stream capability and D568 routes SSE through adapter-local parsing. A strict lifecycle keeps driver behavior testable and prevents each concrete runtime from inventing status, retry, parser, buffering, or scheduler semantics. Head-before-chunk lets adapters such as from_sse validate content type/status before parsing bytes, while terminal-once and cancel fencing match existing EnvironmentDrivers callback discipline. Explicitly allowing synchronous callbacks preserves existing Rust driver patterns while requiring adapters to fence semantic rejection safely. Keeping status acceptance in typed adapters preserves typed graph-visible source semantics and avoids turning LocalHttpStreamDriver into a generic application protocol authority.

layer: L6 / Rust from_sse adapter-local parser contract / B72-D568-D569
question: What SSE parsing and validation contract should Rust from_sse use when consuming LocalHttpStreamDriver chunks without making the parser a public runtime or protocol surface?
decision: Rust from_sse's HTTP-stream fallback uses an adapter-local SSE parser following the standard event-stream line model: chunks are accumulated across boundaries, UTF-8 text is decoded incrementally, CRLF/CR/LF line endings are accepted, comment lines beginning with ':' are ignored, field lines split on the first ':', a single leading space after ':' is stripped, blank lines dispatch the current event only when at least one data line is present, repeated data fields join with '\n', event sets SseEvent.event, id sets SseEvent.id, retry parses a non-negative decimal u64 into retry_ms and ignores malformed retry fields, and unknown fields are ignored. On stream Complete, an unterminated buffered event with data is dispatched before COMPLETE; unterminated partial lines without a blank dispatch are ignored unless they complete a data-bearing event according to the accumulated parser state. The HTTP-stream fallback accepts 2xx response heads with content-type text/event-stream allowing parameters such as charset; unacceptable status/content-type, invalid UTF-8, or parser overflow emits adapter ERROR and cancels/ignores the stream per D569. The parser is private to from_sse, exposes no public parser type, no generic text/event stream source, no retry/reconnect scheduling, no Last-Event-ID management, no provider/runtime authority, and no protocol/conformance behavior.
rationale: D568 keeps SSE parsing adapter-local over the D567 HTTP stream fallback, while D569 separates transport lifecycle from typed adapter semantics. Locking the parser contract prevents each implementation from choosing different event dispatch, retry, UTF-8, content-type, and terminal-flush behavior. Keeping retry as parsed data only respects D130-D132 resilience boundaries and avoids hidden reconnect scheduling. Keeping Last-Event-ID and public parser APIs out of scope avoids turning from_sse into a broader event-stream runtime or provider adapter.

layer: L6 / TS memory, scoring, and WorkItem-agentic-memory package boundaries
question: How should @graphrefly/ts place reusable scoring, semantic-memory, WorkItem runtime, agentic-memory, and the default WorkItem-memory bridge without collapsing horizontal families into graph/core/orchestration or vertical solutions into each other?
decision: @graphrefly/ts should treat scoring as a top-level reusable application-infrastructure/pattern family under src/scoring, not graph/scoring or graph/policies. The scoring model is subjects plus signals plus explicit policy facts/options producing scored or ranked views; it must not become substrate graph policy, hidden routing authority, model/provider runtime, storage hydration, or WorkItem/agent-specific workflow. Memory is a horizontal family under src/memory, with folder-first semantic memory under src/memory/semantic/{types,retrieval,store,history,knowledge-graph}. Lower semantic-memory bundles such as semanticMemoryStoreBundle and fragmentHistoryBundle belong to this memory family and expose graph-visible fragments, retrieval/store/history/KG facts, status, issues, cursors, and policy material; they must not revive reactiveFactStore, own SQLite/LLM/provider adapters, own storage hydration/restore, schedule timers, mutate graph topology, or create AgenticMemoryRecord values. solutions/agentic-memory remains independent from WorkItem, and solutions/work-item remains independent from AgenticMemory; orchestration keeps only truly generic Layer C primitives. Existing work-item-runtime-* material should migrate toward solutions/work-item/runtime as the WorkItem-owned runtime/recipe surface while preserving only intentionally experimental package exposure during the migration, not creating legacy compatibility aliases or a dependency on agentic memory. The default integration between WorkItem and memory lives in solutions/agentic-work-item-memory as a replaceable recipe/bridge template over declared graph-visible facts, with replaceable policy, mapper, context source, and admission stages. It may compose WorkItem projections/evidence/context facts with AgenticMemory proposal/admission facts, but neither WorkItem nor orchestration may directly write AgenticMemoryRecord truth.
rationale: D158 separates horizontal semantic-memory patterns from vertical agentic-memory solutions and forbids hidden storage/runtime ownership. D164-D172 keep the AgenticMemoryRecord envelope, retention, consolidation execution, and persistence sidecars solution-layer and explicit. D182/D189/D207/D217/D235/D239 keep WorkItem domain state, effect runs, request flows, evidence mapping, and action application separated by graph-visible facts and policy/admission stages. D194/D195 make context assembly generic rather than WorkItem-owned. D349 and D566 keep orchestration/application infrastructure generic while deferring vertical agent/product semantics. This decision records the concrete TypeScript package/source layout and bridge boundary so implementation can migrate experimental WorkItem runtime material without turning graph, orchestration, memory, WorkItem, or agentic memory into each other's owner.

layer: L6 / AgenticMemory proposal admission spine and typed context attribution
question: How should new agentic-memory records be proposed from WorkItem, consolidation, retrieval, or other solution flows without letting any producer directly write record truth or losing context attribution needed for credit assignment?
decision: AgenticMemoryRecordProposal is the generic proposal/admission spine for creating or changing agentic-memory record truth. It is not consolidation-only draft material. Consolidation executors, WorkItem-memory bridge recipes, human review flows, retrieval feedback, import/migration flows, and other solution mappers may emit proposal facts carrying candidate record material, sourceRefs, policyRefs, reason/status material, and idempotency/correlation coordinates. An explicit admission projector or replaceable admission policy consumes proposals plus current records/fragments/context/evidence and emits admitted, rejected, needs-review, status, issues, audit, and cursor facts. Only admitted proposal/application facts may become AgenticMemoryRecord values through the agentic-memory solution's owned record application path. WorkItem code, WorkItem runtime recipes, generic orchestration, context assembly, scoring, semantic-memory store/history bundles, retrieval bundles, and consolidation executors must not directly append or mutate AgenticMemoryRecord. Context material used for proposal, ranking, packing, mapping, and credit assignment should carry typed attribution including fragmentId, recordId, queryId, rank, score, truncation, and sourceRefs where applicable. These fields are provenance and evaluation material only: they are not storage keys, provider handles, graph node handles, permission grants, hidden hydration authority, or protocol metadata.
rationale: D164 keeps AgenticMemoryRecord as a solution envelope projected down to lower fragments, while lower patterns do not consume or require the envelope. D171 already states consolidation execution may project proposed record draft material but must not directly create records; this decision generalizes that proposal/admission spine beyond consolidation. D189/D207/D217/D235/D239 require WorkItem effects and mappings to re-enter as evidence, proposals, policies, or domain actions rather than direct mutation. D194/D195 establish generic context contribution/assembly with source refs, ranking, truncation, and materialization outside provider-specific prompt rendering. Typed attribution gives retrieval, context packing, WorkItem-memory bridges, and admission policy enough credit-assignment data without weakening graph-visible causality or storage/runtime boundaries.

layer: L6 / scoring primitives, memory proposal lifecycle, and typed attribution API shape
question: What minimal public API shape should @graphrefly/ts expose for reusable scoring, AgenticMemory record proposals, typed context attribution, and WorkItem-memory score mapping?
decision: @graphrefly/ts scoring uses generic ScoreSubject, ScoreSignal, ScorePolicy, and ScoredView facts. ScoreSignal is a graph-visible DATA fact with subject identity, open dimension string, numeric value, optional confidence/weight/time validity, sourceRefs, policyRefs, and metadata; reviewer outcomes, executor outcomes, and WorkItem evidence map into ScoreSignal through explicit mappers rather than becoming scoring-owned enums. AgenticMemoryRecordProposal is a solution-level proposal fact with candidate record material, sourceRefs, policyRefs, reason/status material, idempotency/correlation coordinates, and an explicit admission/application lifecycle before AgenticMemoryRecord truth changes. Context attribution is a typed DTO carrying fragmentId, recordId, queryId, rank, score, truncation, and sourceRefs where applicable, and may appear on AgenticMemory context entries, packed context entries, and ContextContribution-compatible bridge facts. WorkItem-memory integration emits generic ScoreSignal and AgenticMemoryRecordProposal facts only from replaceable bridge recipes; WorkItem, scoring, context assembly, and lower memory bundles do not directly write AgenticMemoryRecord.
rationale: This refines D571 and D572 into minimal public type shapes while preserving graph-visible DATA facts, explicit policy/admission, typed provenance for credit assignment, and independence between scoring, AgenticMemory, WorkItem, context assembly, and lower semantic-memory bundles. It also preserves D197 by requiring score-based ranking to consume explicit score data rather than invent hidden scores.

layer: L6 / Cross-runtime compound fact identity encoding
question: How should TS, Rust, and Python encode generated compound fact ids and keys without colliding on open user/domain strings or confusing them with graph topology mount paths?
decision: Generated compound fact ids, admission ids, correlation keys, dedupe keys, and other graph-visible or stable application-infrastructure keys outside graph topology and mount paths must use a canonical tuple encoding over ordered string coordinates. Graph path and mount path material keeps its existing mount-aware :: path syntax and is the only sanctioned use of :: as a structural path delimiter. The canonical tuple encoding is deterministic, injective over ordered coordinates, safe for open strings containing colons or delimiter-like material, and should be hidden behind local helper functions rather than handwritten concatenation. User-authored opaque ids remain opaque strings; this decision applies when the library derives a compound id/key from multiple coordinates. The convention applies across @graphrefly/ts, @graphrefly/rust, and @graphrefly/py as their corresponding generated compound ids/keys are implemented or migrated. Tuple-encoded ids are data vocabulary only: they are not graph paths, provider handles, storage handles, permission grants, routing authority, graph policy, protocol metadata, or runtime handles.
rationale: The scoring and AgenticMemory proposal/admission slices exposed a real collision class: open ids such as policyId, proposalId, subjectId, workItemId, and domain refs may themselves contain colon-like separators, while old generated ids often joined coordinates with :. Switching those generated ids to :: would collide with the already-locked topology/mount path meaning used by describe(), observe(), graph subtree matching, and mount-aware node ids. Existing TS internals already show safer compound-key precedent with nonordinary delimiters for private maps, but graph-visible/stable facts need a portable, inspectable, cross-runtime encoding. Canonical tuple encoding preserves open string coordinates, keeps graph paths visually and semantically distinct, supports deterministic tests and audit facts, and avoids creating a provider/storage/runtime or protocol concept. This refines D571-D573 without changing protocol tiers, messages, ctx, batch, graph topology semantics, WorkItem ownership, AgenticMemory ownership, or cross-language behavioral conformance rules.

layer: L6 / Tuple encoding helper boundary for private storage and runtime codecs
question: When private storage/runtime code needs collision-safe compound keys, should it reuse the public D574 identity helpers directly or hide the same tuple mechanics behind area-local helpers?
decision: D574 identity helpers remain semantic helpers for generated graph-visible fact ids, admission/correlation/dedupe ids, and stable application-infrastructure DATA vocabulary. Private storage physical keys, storage namespace codecs, content-addressed KV keys, dispatcher/profile map keys, and other runtime-local lookup keys may reuse the same deterministic JSON tuple mechanics for collision safety, but only behind area-local helper names and docs such as storagePhysicalKey, contentAddressedStorageKey, or dispatcherHandleStatKey. Those local helpers must not describe their outputs as graph-visible facts, graph paths, provider handles, storage handles, permission grants, routing authority, graph policy, protocol metadata, hydration authority, or runtime handles. Public graph path and mount path material continues to use the existing :: syntax only for topology paths. User-authored opaque ids remain opaque strings and are included as tuple coordinates only when the library derives a new compound key from them.
rationale: D574 solved real collision bugs in generated compound facts, but QA exposed an adjacent semantic risk: directly importing a generic identity helper inside storage backends or dispatcher internals makes private physical/runtime keys look like the same vocabulary as graph-visible DATA fact ids. D82 keeps storage passive and adapter-owned, D7 keeps handles pure data but not graph facts, and D39 keeps profiling counters on dispatcher internals rather than thin nodes. Area-local helpers preserve the collision-safe encoding and cross-runtime determinism while keeping ownership and authority explicit. This refines D574 without changing protocol tiers, messages, ctx, batch, graph topology semantics, storage restore/hydration scope, WorkItem ownership, AgenticMemory ownership, or behavioral conformance rules.

layer: L6 / AgenticMemory record application family boundary / D571-D573 follow-up
question: How should AgenticMemory proposals become record truth across admission, application, consolidation, attribution, and WorkItem-memory bridge slices without letting adjacent families directly write AgenticMemoryRecord values?
decision: AgenticMemory record application is an AgenticMemory-owned family boundary after proposal admission. AgenticMemoryRecordProposal remains the generic proposal/admission spine for candidate record creation or change, and admission emits admitted, rejected, needs-review, status, issues, audit, and cursor DATA facts only; admission does not append, replace, or mutate AgenticMemoryRecord truth by itself. The record application projector is a separate AgenticMemory-owned slice that may later consume admitted, issue-free, proposal-compatible application material plus current records/policy/idempotency evidence and emit new AgenticMemoryRecord truth or application status/issues; no interim slice may compensate by writing records directly. Typed context attribution is DATA/provenance DTO material, carrying fragmentId, recordId, queryId, rank, score, truncation, sourceRefs, and related evaluation coordinates where applicable; it is not storage key material, permission/capability authority, graph handles, provider/runtime handles, or protocol metadata. Consolidation executors and existing proposed-record draft material should migrate toward AgenticMemoryRecordProposal-compatible facts before record truth changes, preserving D171's executor boundary. The WorkItem-memory bridge remains a replaceable recipe under solutions/agentic-work-item-memory: it may emit generic ScoreSignal facts and AgenticMemoryRecordProposal-compatible facts from declared WorkItem evidence/context/outcome inputs, but WorkItem, scoring, context assembly, semantic-memory bundles, orchestration, and bridge recipes must not directly append or mutate AgenticMemoryRecord. This decision refines D571-D573 and follows the Workspace D425-D430/D434/D437 pattern of generic proposal/admission coordinates plus family-owned application/outcome facts. It introduces no protocol tier, message, ctx.up/down, graph verb, batch, storage-restore, or cross-language conformance change.
rationale: D164-D172 keep AgenticMemoryRecord truth solution-owned and separate from lower semantic-memory patterns, storage, retention, consolidation execution, KG projection, and persistence sidecars. D171 allows consolidation to project proposed draft material but forbids direct record creation. D572-D573 already generalize proposals, admission, typed attribution, ScoreSignal, and WorkItem-memory mapping, but the TS implementation needs one umbrella boundary so slices do not fill the missing application projector by mutating records directly. The Workspace proposal family precedent proves the clean shape: generic proposal/admission/idempotency/audit mechanics stay reusable, while the family owner records domain truth and outcomes. Keeping typed attribution and scores as ordinary DATA/provenance preserves D194-D197 context/scoring inspectability, and keeping WorkItem integration recipe-only preserves D189/D217/D235/D239's evidence-first and policy/application boundaries.

layer: L6 / AgenticMemory record application projector API shape
question: What public application projector shape should turn admitted AgenticMemory proposal material into AgenticMemoryRecord truth without mutating records imperatively or smuggling update/idempotency/storage semantics?
decision: AgenticMemory record application ships as an AgenticMemory-owned projection bundle and pure helper consuming current AgenticMemoryRecord records, AgenticMemoryRecordAdmission facts, an application policy, and optional graph-visible application/idempotency history. The projector applies only locally valid admissions with state admitted; rejected or needs-review admissions are skipped with decision/audit material, not protocol errors. The first slice is create-only: candidate records may be appended only when their record id and fragment id do not conflict with current records or earlier applied candidates in the same evaluation, and targetRecordId must be absent or equivalent to the candidate record id. Replace/update/patch semantics are deferred to a later design gate. Idempotency is a hard DATA gate only when evidence is present: repeated admissionId or idempotencyKey with matching material is skipped as already-applied, while conflicting reuse is a DATA issue. The projector emits a full next records snapshot plus appliedRecords, applicationDecisions, status, issues, audit, and cursor facts; it does not mutate input records, own storage, perform hydration, call providers/runtimes, depend on WorkItem, or change protocol tiers/messages/ctx/batch.
rationale: D576 locks application as the AgenticMemory-owned boundary after admission, while D572-D573 make proposals/admissions generic DATA facts and forbid adjacent families from writing AgenticMemoryRecord truth. A create-only first projector keeps the truth-writing path small and testable, preserves current admission/consolidation bundle precedent, avoids prematurely locking update merge semantics, and keeps idempotency explicit as graph-visible evidence rather than hidden storage state.

layer: L6 / AgenticMemory record replacement application semantics
question: How should AgenticMemory record application extend beyond create-only without smuggling patch/merge/storage semantics or weakening graph-visible idempotency?
decision: AgenticMemory record application v2 adds an explicit DATA operation vocabulary with create and replace. Create preserves D577 semantics. Replace is a full-record replacement only: targetRecordId is required, the target record must exist, candidateMaterial.record.id must equal targetRecordId, and the candidate record is the complete next AgenticMemoryRecord truth. Partial update/patch material is not accepted by the application projector; upstream mappers may produce a full replacement candidate, while true patch semantics require a later design gate. Replace must carry explicit lineage to the prior record/fragment through candidate fragment parent/source material or sourceRefs/evidenceRefs; the projector does not silently inherit provenance. A changed replacement fragment must use a non-conflicting new fragment id; reusing the prior fragment id is valid only when the fragment material is equivalent. Application decisions, audit, and graph-visible evidence include operation and operationVersion coordinates so idempotency never conflates create and replace. Invalid targets, unsupported operations, missing lineage, duplicate/conflicting record or fragment ids, and idempotency conflicts emit DATA issues/status/audit rather than protocol ERROR. The projector still owns no storage, hydration, provider/runtime, WorkItem dependency, permission handle, or protocol behavior.
rationale: D577 intentionally shipped create-only to avoid prematurely locking update semantics. Full-record replace is the smallest next truth-writing operation that preserves D572/D573 proposal/admission lifecycle, D576 AgenticMemory-owned application, and graph-visible replay/audit. Deferring partial patch keeps schema/merge/delete semantics out of the application projector until explicitly designed, while operation/version coordinates keep idempotency evidence honest across future operation expansion.

layer: L6 / AgenticMemory application material identity and operation-scoped status
question: How should AgenticMemory application idempotency and status remain graph-visible as create/replace operations expand without relying only on ids or collapsing mixed-operation evaluations?
decision: AgenticMemory record application evidence adds a DATA-only material identity for the complete candidate application material. The material identity is derived from a canonical strict-data frame containing operation, operationVersion, targetRecordId, and the full next AgenticMemoryRecord candidate, using deterministic field ordering and canonical encodings such as decimal bigint strings. Idempotency matching requires both the operation/version/id coordinate key and material identity to match; coordinate reuse with different material identity is a DATA idempotency conflict. Operation-scoped application status is exposed as a read-model over application decisions, with one status summary per operation and operationVersion, while aggregate status remains available for whole-evaluation health. These identities and statuses are DTO/data-only and do not introduce storage, hydration, provider/runtime, permission, WorkItem, graph handle, protocol, patch, or merge semantics.
rationale: D577 and D578 require graph-visible idempotency evidence and operation/version coordinates, but replace makes full-record material identity significant. Relying only on record and fragment ids trusts upstream id discipline too much and can conflate divergent replacements. A canonical material identity makes replay/conflict behavior auditable without adding hidden persistence. Operation-scoped status avoids an ambiguous single operation field for mixed create/replace evaluations while preserving the aggregate cursor.

layer: L6 / AgenticMemory complete-next-record update operation
question: What first update semantics should AgenticMemory record application add after create/replace without collapsing into patch/merge or a cross-family mutation vocabulary?
decision: AgenticMemory record application may add an update operation as a complete-next-record operation only. create, update, and replace are AgenticMemory-local application operations aligned with the shared proposal/admission/application pattern; they are not a new cross-family generic mutation vocabulary and do not reuse WorkItem patch semantics. update consumes admitted proposal-compatible material containing a full AgenticMemoryRecord candidate for an existing targetRecordId, requires candidate.record.id to equal targetRecordId, requires the target record to exist, and requires explicit lineage to the prior record or fragment. update applies by replacing the target slot with the complete candidate record, but it is not a patch, merge document, partial field update, hydration, reconstruction, or storage replay mechanism. Idempotency and prior evidence use operation/version/target/material identity coordinates; matching material skips as already-applied and divergent coordinate reuse is a DATA idempotency conflict. True patch/merge semantics require a later design decision.
rationale: D577 deferred update/patch, D578 locked replace as full-record replacement, and D579 made complete material identity operation-scoped. D425-D430/D434/D437 provide the reusable family pattern: generic proposal/admission coordinates plus family-owned application/outcome facts, not a universal mutation enum or arbitrary fact emitter. A complete-next-record update gives producers a semantically honest way to express evolution of an existing AgenticMemory record while preserving the AgenticMemory-owned application boundary and avoiding premature patch/merge semantics.

layer: L6 / WorkItem-memory mapper bridge recipe
question: How should WorkItem evidence integrate with AgenticMemory without letting WorkItem, scoring, context assembly, or bridge recipes write AgenticMemoryRecord truth?
decision: WorkItem-memory integration is a mapper-only recipe under @graphrefly/ts/solutions/agentic-work-item-memory. The bridge consumes declared WorkItem projection, evidence, outcome, context, DATA mapping policy, and optional explicit AgenticMemory candidate material facts, and emits generic ScoreSignal facts plus AgenticMemoryRecordProposal-compatible facts with sourceRefs, policyRefs, idempotency/correlation coordinates, status, issues, audit, and cursor material. It does not admit proposals, apply record truth, mutate AgenticMemoryRecord, mutate WorkItem, own scoring semantics, call providers/runtimes/storage/hydration, or introduce protocol/spec behavior. AgenticMemory and WorkItem remain independent; the bridge may depend on both as a solution recipe, but neither family core depends on the bridge.
rationale: D572-D573/D576 lock AgenticMemoryRecordProposal as the generic proposal spine and forbid adjacent families from writing AgenticMemoryRecord truth. WorkItem outcomes should re-enter memory as evidence, score signals, and proposals, preserving policy/application ownership and keeping scoring dimensions open rather than WorkItem-owned enums. Keeping the bridge mapper-only follows the Workspace proposal family pattern while avoiding storage, runtime, provider, WorkItem mutation, scoring ownership, and protocol drift.

layer: L6 / WorkItem-memory mapper bridge v0 API and coordinate shape
question: What concrete v0 API shape should the D581 WorkItem-memory mapper-only bridge expose without adding callback mappers, generic mutation semantics, or silent candidate-choice authority?
decision: The D581 WorkItem-memory bridge v0 is a DATA-only solution recipe under @graphrefly/ts/solutions/agentic-work-item-memory that consumes current declared WorkItem projections, a DATA mapping policy, optional WorkItem evidence/outcome/context inputs, and optional bridge-wrapped explicit AgenticMemory candidate material facts. The bridge emits only generic ScoreSignal facts, AgenticMemoryRecordProposal-compatible facts, and bridge-local status, issue, audit, and cursor read-model facts. The mapping policy is serializable DATA with score and record proposal mapping rules; it must not contain callback functions, provider/runtime/storage handles, graph handles, permission authority, hydration/replay behavior, scoring ownership, admission/application authority, WorkItem mutation authority, or a generic mutation DSL. Explicit candidate material is wrapped by a bridge-local input DTO carrying candidateId, workItemId, source/policy refs, and metadata so the bridge can derive stable proposal, idempotency, correlation, and causation coordinates. Generated ids and keys use D574 tuple helpers over policyId, workItem coordinates, source coordinates, mapping rule or candidate id, operation, and target/candidate record identity; handwritten delimiter concatenation is not allowed for generated bridge ids. Bridge read-model names stay bridge-local, such as AgenticWorkItemMemoryBridgeStatus, AgenticWorkItemMemoryBridgeIssue, AgenticWorkItemMemoryBridgeAuditEntry, and AgenticWorkItemMemoryBridgeCursor, and they must not reuse AgenticMemory admission/application lifecycle names such as admitted, applied, already-applied, or rejected as bridge authority. If an explicit candidate and a policy-generated candidate map to the same bridge coordinate with identical material, the bridge emits one proposal and records duplicate suppression in audit; if they map to the same coordinate with different material, the bridge emits a DATA candidate-conflict issue and emits no proposal for that coordinate. The bridge does not choose a winning candidate silently. Complex candidate generation that cannot be described by the DATA policy should be produced upstream as explicit candidate material before entering the bridge.
rationale: D581 locks the WorkItem-memory integration as mapper-only but leaves the v0 DTO, policy, coordinate, and conflict details open. A concrete DATA-only shape preserves D572-D573/D576 proposal/admission/application boundaries, D574 collision-safe generated identity, D580's AgenticMemory-local operation vocabulary, and the independence of WorkItem, scoring, context assembly, and AgenticMemory. Rejecting callback mappers keeps the recipe serializable and inspectable. Wrapping explicit candidates ties them to WorkItem/source coordinates without letting raw candidate material become hidden truth. Treating explicit-vs-generated material divergence as a DATA issue follows the no-autonomous-decisions value and avoids implicit precedence rules that would silently choose memory truth.

layer: L6 / AgenticMemory admission policy source projection boundary
question: Where should AgenticMemory admission policies come from as WorkItem-memory, consolidation, retrieval feedback, human review, and planner flows move from example wiring into application-level composition?
decision: AgenticMemory admission policy sourcing is an AgenticMemory-owned DATA projection boundary. Application code may provide static policy DATA, workspace policy facts, human-review policy material, planner-suggested policy material, or other producer-specific policy material, but any reusable projection that normalizes or selects an AgenticMemoryRecordAdmissionPolicy belongs to the AgenticMemory solution family, not the WorkItem-memory bridge, WorkItem core, scoring, storage, provider/runtime, or protocol layers. Such policy projection may emit the selected admission policy plus policy-local status, issues, audit, and cursor facts. It must not admit proposals, emit AgenticMemoryRecordAdmission truth, mutate AgenticMemoryRecord values, override proposal material, call providers/runtimes/storage/hydration, carry graph/node handles, grant permissions, or introduce a generic policy engine. WorkItem-memory recipe inputs may consume the resulting policy node as ordinary DATA, preserving D581/D582 mapper-only bridge authority and D572/D576 admission/application ownership.
rationale: D572/D576 make proposal admission explicit and AgenticMemory-owned, while D581/D582 keep the WorkItem-memory bridge mapper-only. The D583 design review surfaced that static policy DATA is enough for examples but application-level flows need a visible source/selection boundary before admission. Placing that boundary in AgenticMemory keeps policy normalization inspectable and reusable across WorkItem-memory, consolidation, retrieval feedback, imports, and human review without allowing producers to directly decide admission outcomes or smuggle runtime/storage authority into the bridge.

layer: L6 / AgenticMemory application evidence and history projection boundary
question: How should AgenticMemory application evidence and history feed idempotency without making application state hidden, self-feeding, or storage-owned?
decision: AgenticMemory application evidence/history is an AgenticMemory-owned DATA projection boundary. Reusable helpers may validate, aggregate, and project AgenticMemoryRecordApplicationEvidence facts into AgenticMemoryRecordApplicationPriorEvidence for the existing application projector, and may project application decisions into appendable evidence facts for future evaluations. Current-evaluation application decisions must not synchronously feed back into the same application evaluation's priorEvidence input; they may only become future prior evidence through an explicit graph/event/storage boundary or later evaluation input. Evidence/history projections may emit status, issues, audit, and cursor facts, but they do not apply records, admit proposals, persist storage, hydrate records, call providers/runtimes, own hidden schedulers, or change idempotency semantics. Storage adapters and hosts may persist or reload evidence facts outside the sync core, then re-enter as ordinary DATA.
rationale: D577/D579 make idempotency evidence graph-visible DATA and operation/material-identity-scoped, while D580 keeps update as complete-next-record rather than replay or merge. The D583 design review identified a real next-step gap: application recipes can already accept priorEvidence, but no owned source projects durable or cross-evaluation evidence. A separate AgenticMemory evidence/history projection keeps idempotency auditable and reusable while avoiding a same-wave feedback cycle, hidden storage state, or bridge-owned application truth.

layer: L6 / AgenticMemory record hydration and storage boundary
question: What owns durable AgenticMemory record hydration/storage once application emits new record snapshots?
decision: Durable AgenticMemory record hydration/storage is outside the WorkItem-memory bridge and outside the record application projector. AgenticMemory may expose passive, DATA-only snapshot/store-frame/codec helpers for AgenticMemoryRecord arrays, application decisions, and application evidence, but storage I/O, loading, persistence, compaction, and backend-specific durability remain adapter/host-owned and occur outside the sync wave core. Hydrated records re-enter AgenticMemory admission/application as ordinary records DATA nodes or graph restore/bootstrap inputs; application output records are graph-visible next snapshots, not durable commit acknowledgements. Store-frame or snapshot helpers must not mutate live records, bypass admission/application, call providers/runtimes, grant permissions, carry storage handles as graph facts, synthesize missing lineage, replay patches, or turn storage restore into AgenticMemory truth mutation. Any future hot hydration or storage-as-commit-barrier semantics require a separate reviewed design and, if protocol-observable, a spec-amend route.
rationale: D82/D83/D161 keep storage passive, async loading outside the sync core, and restore/hydration distinct from ordinary graph waves, while D576/D577 keep record truth changes AgenticMemory-application-owned. The D583 design review surfaced that treating application.records as durable truth would collapse graph DATA snapshots with persistence commits. This boundary lets AgenticMemory add useful codecs and store-frame material without moving storage ownership into bridge or application helpers and without weakening restore/hydration authority.

layer: L6 / AgenticMemory complete-next-record change materialization and patch-merge deferral
question: How should update/replace sources and future patch/merge requests enter AgenticMemory application without turning application into a generic mutation DSL?
decision: AgenticMemory application remains complete-next-record application over the existing create, replace, and update operations. Producers may propose replace or update only by supplying AgenticMemoryRecordProposal-compatible candidate material containing the full next AgenticMemoryRecord, targetRecordId where required, operation/version coordinates, and explicit lineage to the prior record or fragment as required by D580. Reusable upstream materializers may live in the AgenticMemory solution family to convert domain-specific change intent plus current records into complete-next-record candidate material and proposal facts, emitting materializer-local status, issues, audit, and cursor facts. These materializers must not apply records, admit proposals, mutate WorkItem or AgenticMemory truth, define a cross-family mutation vocabulary, or let the WorkItem-memory bridge interpret patch/merge semantics. True patch or merge operations are deferred to a later design decision and must either materialize into complete next records before application or explicitly amend AgenticMemory-local application semantics; they must not be added as a generic mutation DSL or storage replay mechanism.
rationale: D580 already locks update as a complete-next-record operation and explicitly defers true patch/merge semantics. The D583 design review clarified that the next expansion should focus on where update/replace candidate material comes from, not on widening the application enum prematurely. A materialization boundary lets planners, consolidation, retrieval feedback, or WorkItem-derived flows express evolution while preserving D572/D576 proposal/admission/application ownership, D579 material identity, D581/D582 bridge limits, and the no-autonomous-decisions rule for conflicting material.

layer: L6 / AgenticMemory x WorkItem application composition recipe
question: Where should reusable WorkItem-to-AgenticMemory admission/application composition live without weakening the D581/D582 mapper-only WorkItem-memory bridge boundary?
decision: Reusable WorkItem-to-AgenticMemory admission/application composition belongs in a separate solution-level cross-family composition surface, not in the WorkItem-memory mapper bridge namespace and not in AgenticMemory core. The WorkItem-memory bridge remains mapper-only and emits only ScoreSignal, AgenticMemoryRecordProposal-compatible facts, and bridge-local read models. The composition recipe may wire the WorkItem-memory bridge outputs into AgenticMemory-owned admission and application helpers, and may expose the resulting admission/application read models, but it does not own admission policy selection, application truth mutation, storage, hydration, providers, runtimes, WorkItem mutation, or application evidence self-feedback. Current-evaluation application decisions must not be synchronously wired into the same application evaluation's priorEvidence; any application evidence/history enters as ordinary external DATA from an explicit boundary or later evaluation input.
rationale: D581/D582 intentionally keep the WorkItem-memory bridge mapper-only, while D572/D576/D577 make AgenticMemory proposal admission and record application AgenticMemory-owned boundaries. A real application recipe is useful, but placing it under agentic-work-item-memory makes the bridge namespace appear to broker admission/application authority, and placing it under agentic-memory would make AgenticMemory core depend on WorkItem. A separate cross-family composition surface preserves both family boundaries while keeping the graph topology explicit and inspectable.

layer: L6 / AgenticMemory durable fact-log authority
question: If AgenticMemory stored facts must become the durable source of truth, what belongs in the library versus host/userland storage backends?
decision: AgenticMemory may promote a durable committed fact log to the source of truth for durable memory state, but the authority is the canonical committed AgenticMemory fact stream, not an adapter callback, live graph cache, application output snapshot, or backend-specific storage handle. The library owns the canonical fact/store-frame schemas, codecs, ordering and cursor semantics, material identity and idempotency/conflict rules, replay/materialization-from-committed-facts rules, and snapshot/tail-log compaction invariants. Hosts and backend adapters own physical storage backends such as SQLite, IndexedDB, files, or object stores, plus concrete transaction, durability, encryption, retention, backup, scheduling, and deployment consistency policy. Application records, decisions, and evidence become durable truth only after admission/application has emitted graph-visible facts and those facts have been committed to the durable fact log; current AgenticMemory records are derived/materialized from committed facts by AgenticMemory-owned rules. Snapshots are acceleration/compaction artifacts and must be equivalent to a committed fact-log prefix plus tail, not a second competing truth source. Adapter status, issues, audit, cursors, and any future commit result describe fact-log persistence/materialization progress only; they must not apply records, admit proposals, select policy, mutate live graph truth invisibly, synthesize lineage, replay patches as application, or treat raw application output as durable commit acknowledgement. Exact commit-barrier and hot-hydration API semantics remain a separate reviewed design, and any protocol-observable restore/hydration behavior must route through spec-amend before implementation.
rationale: D585 deliberately limited the previous slice to passive store-frame helpers and required a separate reviewed design for hot hydration or storage-as-commit-barrier semantics. The next requirement is stronger: durable stored facts must be allowed to serve as the source of truth without collapsing storage adapters into application projectors or making graph snapshots equal storage commits. Placing canonical fact-log semantics in the library preserves single-source-of-truth, replay determinism, idempotency, conflict handling, and cross-backend portability, while keeping backend durability and operations host-owned as required by D82/D83/D93/D161. Treating snapshots as compaction artifacts rather than competing truth protects D584/D585 evidence and hydration boundaries and keeps committed facts re-entering graph evaluation through explicit DATA/bootstrap/restore boundaries.

layer: L6 / AgenticMemory committed fact-log contract
question: What exact committed fact-log contract, commit-result boundary, and deterministic materialization rules should follow D588 without smuggling in backend-specific storage, hot hydration, or graph commit semantics?
decision: AgenticMemory committed fact-log v0 is an AgenticMemory-owned durable fact contract for AgenticMemory-owned facts only: record material facts, application decision facts, application evidence facts, and derived prior-evidence/history facts. The committed log appends batches of canonical facts, not raw application output snapshots; each fact has a deterministic identity and material identity derived from its family/kind, operation coordinates, source/correlation refs, and canonical strict-data material. Batch commit is first-class: a committed batch becomes visible as a whole or not at all, and partial batch visibility is invalid. Commit results use a closed status vocabulary of committed, duplicate, conflict, rejected, and uncertain. committed means the canonical fact batch is durable in the fact log; duplicate means the same identities and material were already committed idempotently; conflict means an identity was reused with different material; rejected means validation or precondition failure before commit; uncertain means the host/backend cannot prove whether the batch committed and callers must resolve by read/idempotency rather than assuming success or failure. A commit result is not an application acknowledgement, not live graph truth, and not permission to mutate records; it describes durable fact-log persistence only. Cursors denote positions in the AgenticMemory fact stream, not graph wave clocks, application versions, backend row ids, or policy clocks. Reads return committed facts after a cursor in stream order. Deterministic library materializers derive current records and prior evidence from committed facts; backends must not own replay semantics or choose conflict winners. Snapshots are compaction artifacts over a committed fact-log prefix, and snapshot plus tail must materialize identically to replaying the covered prefix plus tail. D589 does not lock SQLite schema, IndexedDB/S3/file semantics, hot hydration, live graph refresh, durable graph batch commit barriers, retention/deletion/redaction, migration, or multi-tenant authorization; those require later reviewed decisions, and protocol-observable restore/hydration changes require spec-amend.
rationale: D588 establishes the canonical committed AgenticMemory fact stream as the durable source of truth while keeping physical storage host-owned. The next implementation needs a precise library contract for what can be appended, how identity/idempotency/conflict behave, what commit results mean, and how facts materialize back into AgenticMemory state. Batch atomic visibility, uncertain commit status, stream cursors, and deterministic materialization are necessary to support real backends without letting adapters become application projectors or treating application outputs as durable truth. Keeping backend schemas, hot hydration, commit barriers, and retention out of D589 preserves the D585/D588 boundary and leaves protocol-observable lifecycle changes to spec-first review.

layer: L6 / AgenticMemory durable-result gate boundary
question: How may AgenticMemory applications observe durable committed fact-log persistence without turning commit results into application acknowledgements, live graph truth, hot hydration, or graph commit barriers?
decision: AgenticMemory may expose a durable-result gate boundary as an AgenticMemory-owned solution-level DATA read model over D589 committed fact-log append/read results. The gate may correlate canonical committed fact batches with fact-log commit results and emit graph-visible durability result, status, issue, audit, and cursor facts. Durable statuses committed and duplicate may allow downstream application workflows to advance by explicit policy; conflict and rejected are terminal durability-attempt failures; uncertain is neither success nor failure and requires explicit read/idempotency resolution. These durability result facts describe only committed fact-log persistence progress. They are not application acknowledgements, not live graph truth, not record mutation authority, not hot hydration, and not graph wave/batch commit barriers. Storage/backend adapters remain host-owned and async outside the sync wave core; concrete backend transaction semantics, SQLite/IndexedDB/S3/file schemas, fsync guarantees, retry scheduling, retention/deletion/redaction, migration, auth, live refresh, and hot hydration remain out of scope. A storage failure may prevent a downstream success-gated workflow from advancing, but it must not retroactively roll back application DATA, admission/application decisions, graph waves, or graph batches. Committed facts re-enter AgenticMemory only through explicit fact-log read plus library-owned materialization, or through later DATA/bootstrap/restore paths governed by existing hydration/restore rules. Any future design that makes fact-log durability a graph commit barrier or protocol-observable restore/hydration behavior must route through spec-amend.
rationale: D93 already permits reactive durable-result gates while rejecting storage durability rollback of graph commits. D588 and D589 establish committed AgenticMemory facts as durable truth but sharply separate fact-log persistence results from application acknowledgement, live graph state, replay authority, backend storage policy, and hydration. D590 gives applications an explicit, inspectable DATA boundary for durable persistence progress without weakening those separations.
