Keeping the gate in the AgenticMemory solution layer preserves canonical fact-log semantics and lets downstream workflows choose whether to wait for durable persistence, while storage remains passive/host-owned and the sync wave core remains free of async durability barriers.

layer: L6 / AgenticMemory fact-log read materialization re-entry boundary
question: How may committed AgenticMemory fact-log reads re-enter AgenticMemory without making backends own replay, live graph truth, hot hydration, or graph restore semantics?
decision: AgenticMemory may expose explicit fact-log read materialization and re-entry helpers as AgenticMemory-owned solution-level DATA projections over D589 committed fact-log read results. The library owns validation, stream-order materialization, status, issues, audit, and cursor facts, and may emit ordinary records, priorEvidence, and evidence DATA for callers to wire into later admission, application, bootstrap, or restore inputs. Backends and storage adapters only supply read results; they do not replay, apply, admit, mutate records, choose conflict winners, hydrate live graph state, refresh subscribers, or own restore/bootstrap semantics. Re-entry is explicit and caller-wired; it is not hot hydration, not live graph truth mutation, not same-evaluation feedback, and not a graph wave/batch commit barrier. Protocol-observable restore/hydration behavior or fact-log durability commit barriers require spec-amend.
rationale: D588 and D589 make committed AgenticMemory facts the durable source of truth and library materialization authoritative, while D585 and D590 keep storage, hot hydration, live refresh, and commit barriers out of scope. A narrow explicit re-entry boundary lets applications read and materialize durable facts safely without granting storage adapters replay authority or changing sync wave semantics. Keeping re-entry as ordinary DATA preserves graph inspectability and leaves backend transaction, retry, retention, fsync, and live-refresh policy to later reviewed adapter designs.

layer: L6 / AgenticMemory committed fact-log backend adapter contract
question: What exact backend adapter contract may AgenticMemory expose for committed fact-log physical storage without granting replay, materialization, restore, or live graph authority?
decision: AgenticMemory may expose a narrow committed fact-log backend adapter contract whose only GraphReFly-facing semantic operations are append canonical committed fact batches and read committed fact results in fact-stream order. Adapters may own physical transactions, durability attempts, storage cursors, backend diagnostics, and environment-specific capabilities, but their public result must normalize to D589 append/read result DATA: committed/duplicate/conflict/rejected/uncertain, fact-stream cursor, issues, and audit. Adapters must not materialize records, replay facts into application state, apply/admit/mutate records, select conflict winners beyond deterministic identity/material equality, hydrate live graphs, refresh subscribers, own restore/bootstrap, expose backend row ids as fact cursors, or act as graph commit barriers. Backend-specific schema, fsync, retry, retention, auth, migration, encryption, and deployment consistency remain adapter/host policy and may appear only as capability/status/issue/audit DATA, not protocol semantics.
rationale: D588-D591 split canonical fact semantics from physical storage. A backend contract lets real adapters exist without making storage the owner of AgenticMemory truth, re-entry, restore, or graph lifecycle.

layer: L6 / AgenticMemory materialized fact-log bootstrap and restore-input boundary
question: How may D591 materialized read DATA feed AgenticMemory bootstrap or restore paths without becoming hot hydration, hidden live mutation, same-evaluation feedback, or a protocol commit barrier?
decision: AgenticMemory may expose explicit bootstrap/re-entry composition helpers that accept already-materialized D591 records, priorEvidence, evidence, status, issues, audit, and cursor DATA and project caller-wirable inputs for later AgenticMemory admission, application, bootstrap, or restore-input flows as ordinary graph DATA. These helpers may validate readiness and partial-read status, expose status/issues/audit/cursor, and require caller-visible wiring. They must not read storage, call backends, mutate existing live graph caches invisibly, refresh subscribers, bypass admission/application ownership, feed current-evaluation application decisions back into the same evaluation, claim restore completion, or create graph wave/batch commit barriers. If a future helper commits materialized facts into graph checkpoint restore/hydration lifecycle, changes restored graph state behind subscribers, gates graph readiness, or creates protocol-observable restore ordering, that is not ordinary D593 DATA integration and must route through spec-amend against R-restore/R-snapshot.
rationale: D591 permits committed facts to re-enter as ordinary DATA, while R-restore already owns lifecycle restore semantics. This decision locks the safe composition lane and prevents bootstrap convenience from becoming hot hydration, storage-owned restore, or hidden graph mutation.

layer: L6 / AgenticMemory concrete committed fact-log backend policy
question: What concrete backend policy may AgenticMemory reference adapters use before SQLite, IndexedDB, or file implementations without changing D589-D593 semantics?
decision: AgenticMemory concrete committed fact-log reference backends may implement the existing D592 backend adapter contract directly; no separate reference-backend policy DTO is required before the first concrete adapter. A concrete backend may choose physical schema, transaction boundaries, storage keys, writer mode, and durability attempt strategy, but its only GraphReFly-facing semantic operations remain append canonical committed fact batches and read committed facts in fact-stream order. Public append/read outputs must normalize to D589 result DATA. Backend fsync or transaction guarantees, writer mode, storage cursors, row ids, health, and capabilities may appear only as backend status, issue, and audit DATA. The first reference backend should be single-writer unless it uses an explicit passive conditional-create capability; multi-writer correctness, retention, deletion, redaction, migration, encryption, auth, retry schedulers, hot refresh, restore lifecycle, and graph commit barriers remain separate reviewed designs. Backend row ids and storage cursors must never be fact-log cursors, and uncertain append remains unresolved until explicit read/idempotency resolution.
rationale: D588-D593 define canonical committed facts, D589 statuses/cursors, D590 durable-result gates, D591 materialization, D592 backend adapters, and D593 bootstrap re-entry. Concrete backends need a narrow policy lock for transaction, durability, cursor, and writer-mode claims so the first SQLite, IndexedDB, or file implementation can proceed directly against D592 without smuggling in application acknowledgement, backend replay, hot hydration, live graph mutation, or graph commit-barrier semantics.

layer: L6 / Canvas bounded widget draft review and host admission correlation
question: How may Canvas let a user review and accept or reject an AI-generated or pasted widget draft without owning draft lifecycle, renderer execution, admission, persistence, or pinned truth?
decision: Canvas may consume a host-supplied bounded widget draft review DTO containing an opaque draft id, immutable revision, workspace and target refs, admitted D417 binding preview, D420 renderer admission preview, data-only sandbox/readiness posture, provenance summaries, and expiry/staleness status. Canvas owns only transient selection and review UI. An accept or reject action clone-emits a D519 typed data-only intent carrying caller-supplied intent/idempotency material and exact draft id, revision, workspace, target, and requested presentation refs. Reject requests a host decision; it is not deletion. The host owns draft generation, identity, immutable revisioning, authorization, expiry, retention, privacy, conflict handling, idempotency/deduplication, renderer trust and registry, admission, audit, persistence, and correlation of the decision to the exact draft revision. Canvas must not optimistically pin, infer admission from a click, resolve version conflicts, execute generated source, create iframe/worker/postMessage runtimes, install packages, call registries, or mutate WorkItems or graph truth. Only host-admitted D538/D539 pinned composition or D555 rejection/status material becomes visible product state. Stale, expired, malformed, blocked, unverifiable, mismatched-workspace, mismatched-target, mismatched-renderer, or mismatched-revision material fails closed with disabled actions or diagnostics and no fallback selection. Drafts and pins remain product presentation overlays; real graph inspection under D564 stays primary topology truth.
rationale: D417/D420 keep component binding and renderer admission inert, D519 defines typed caller-owned intent handoff, D538/D539 keep pinned presentation host/user-admitted, and D555 covers host-derived status. A dedicated lock is still required to prevent the new review journey from hiding generated-draft lifecycle, TOCTOU/version conflict, admission, or optimistic pin authority inside Canvas. Exact immutable-revision correlation provides a bounded host handoff while preserving runtime, persistence, audit, and graph-truth ownership outside Canvas.

layer: L6 / Canvas exact-correlation eligibility graph boundary / D595 and M6 application
question: Where must Canvas compute exact identity/version correlation and fail-closed action eligibility for host-admitted widget-draft and repair-review material?
decision: Canvas exact identity/version correlation, immutable handoff validation, duplicate/conflict material checks, and fail-closed action eligibility are authority-sensitive product derivations and must live in a compact private named @graphrefly/ts graph boundary rather than React predicates, component-local state, or a pure DTO builder. The graph boundary consumes only host-admitted bounded DATA, exposes stable graph, topologyGroup, and node names plus topology()/describe() evidence, and produces an inert eligibility/correlation DTO for a pure display and React shell. Widget-draft review under D595 and the M6 repair/diff review journey must apply this boundary consistently. Row, panel, summary, provenance packaging, and rendering remain DTO-only unless independently graph-worthy; product annotations remain overlays and must not replace real graph truth under D564. Canvas still does not own admission, authorization, conflict resolution, idempotency/deduplication, persistence, runtime execution, provider/storage/credential handles, WorkItem or graph mutation, or optimistic presentation truth. The boundary remains private with no root, focused-surface, or package export expansion; host-admitted D538/D539/D555 material remains the only visible admitted outcome. One-shot bundles own only their declared graph nodes and idempotent release/dispose, with no hidden subscription or retained lifecycle authority.
rationale: D595 requires exact immutable-revision correlation and fail-closed handling, while D564/D565 require authority-sensitive and review-useful Canvas behavior to remain graph-visible without turning DTO assembly into graph towers. The initial M5 implementation labeled a helper that decided exact correlation and accept/reject eligibility as DTO-only, which made the authority classifier inconsistent and risked copying the same predicate into M6 React integration. A small graph boundary plus DTO shell preserves host ownership, makes the decision seam inspectable, keeps presentation assembly inert, and applies the existing GraphReFly/Canvas authority floor without changing protocol or public API.

layer: L6 / Canvas M6 host-admitted repair review input and focused Workbench contract
question: How may a supported Workbench caller supply the immutable repair proposal correlation and admitted current/proposed graph snapshots needed for a real M6 repair/diff review without giving Canvas repair execution or graph authority?
decision: The existing focused @graphrefly/canvas/workspace-canvas-workbench surface may add one bounded data-only host-admitted repair-review input. The input carries proposalId, immutable revision, caller-supplied intentId and idempotencyKey, workspaceId, one exact target ref, and optional current/proposed GraphTopologySnapshot or DescribeSnapshot material derived from real graph inspection. Existing host-command feedback is correlated only by exact intentId and idempotencyKey; missing, duplicate, stale, wrong-workspace, wrong-target, wrong-revision, or mismatched feedback fails closed and cannot enable a decision or claim an admitted outcome. The private M6 graph boundary owns only exact correlation, eligibility, and admission/release-barrier derivation. Current/proposed diff rows, affected-binding rows, host-outcome summaries, provenance packaging, panel rendering, and semantic fallback annotations are pure DTO/display work outside the graph. Current and proposed snapshots remain host-admitted inspection material; Canvas neither creates proposed graph truth from semantic DTOs nor applies the repair. The focused contract adds no new package export path and carries no callbacks, executable values, provider/storage/runtime/credential handles, persistence owner, conflict resolver, WorkItem mutation, graph mutation, or optimistic successor truth. Only a later host-admitted current snapshot may become current graph truth.
rationale: The existing M6 bundle could inspect an optional proposed snapshot internally, but WorkspaceCanvasWorkbench had no supported production input for a caller to provide it, so the product could never leave needs-host-admission and its aggregate feedback counts were not exactly correlated. D596 requires exact correlation in a compact graph boundary, while M6 consumability requires the already-reviewed focused Workbench caller seam to admit the bounded DATA. This focused extension completes the real entry-to-host-outcome journey without creating a new export path or moving execution, persistence, admission, or graph truth into Canvas.

layer: L6 / Canvas M6 proposal and decision-handoff correlation sources / D597 correction
question: How can Canvas verify M6 immutable revision correlation rather than accepting a single host-supplied revision as self-validating?
decision: The focused D597 repair-review input is split into two independent bounded data-only materials: a host-admitted proposal envelope carrying proposalId, immutable revision, workspaceId, exact target ref, and proposed real-graph inspection snapshot; and a decision-handoff envelope carrying the same proposalId, revision, workspaceId, and exact target ref plus caller-supplied intentId and idempotencyKey. The private graph boundary compares every coordinate exactly and also requires the active Workbench workspace to match. Missing, duplicate, stale, wrong-revision, wrong-workspace, or wrong-target-kind/id material fails closed. Current graph truth comes from the already-admitted Topology Lens graph source, not from the repair proposal or handoff envelope. Host feedback correlates only through one exact intentId/idempotencyKey match and cannot repair a proposal/handoff mismatch. The graph retains only request/correlation authority nodes; diff/model/status/provenance and recovery copy are pure DTO/React shell material. Correlation failure must be visibly classified with sanitized recovery guidance and existing typed retry/review affordances. No new export path, execution, persistence, conflict resolution, runtime/provider/storage/credential authority, WorkItem mutation, graph mutation, or optimistic successor truth is authorized.
rationale: QA showed that D597's single revision field could only be checked for presence, not exact equality, and that its workspace and target kind were insufficiently bound. Separating proposal truth from decision handoff creates two independently supplied immutable coordinates for D596 exact correlation, while sourcing current truth from the existing Lens seam prevents foreign repair admission from relabeling current topology. Keeping all display assembly outside the graph completes the approved small-boundary-plus-DTO-shell classification.

layer: L6 / Canvas M6 exact-correlated recovery intent
question: How may M6 offer actionable recovery after correlation failure without selecting the first unrelated ready cockpit intent?
decision: The D598 host-admitted proposal envelope may include one optional bounded recovery material carrying the same proposalId, immutable revision, workspaceId, and exact target kind/id plus one existing data-only typed review/refresh intent. The private correlation boundary validates every recovery coordinate against the proposal envelope and active Workbench workspace. Only one exact correlated recovery intent may be exposed; missing, mismatched, duplicate, disabled, or malformed recovery material fails closed to explanatory guidance with no emitted action. Canvas clone-emits the validated typed intent through the existing Workbench action seam and still owns no refresh execution, admission, persistence, runtime/provider/storage/credential access, WorkItem mutation, graph mutation, or optimistic successor truth. Generic first-ready or first-available intent selection is forbidden. Recovery display and button rendering remain DTO/React shell work outside graph.
rationale: Independent QA found that selecting the first ready review-cockpit intent could emit an unrelated action while claiming to refresh the exact failed proposal revision. Binding one host-admitted recovery intent to the same immutable coordinates preserves actionable failure recovery without adding executable callbacks or moving host authority into Canvas.

layer: L6 / Canvas M6 host-admitted affected material
question: How may M6 identify affected evidence, widgets, and targets without inferring repair impact from unrelated review-cockpit actions?
decision: The D598 proposal envelope may include a bounded affectedMaterial list. Each item is inert strict data with role evidence, widget, or target; one exact WorkspaceTargetRef; and a bounded sanitized label plus optional reason. The list is host-admitted under the proposal envelope's proposalId, immutable revision, workspaceId, and exact repair target coordinates. The private correlation boundary validates size, uniqueness, ref shape, label/reason bounds, and proposal eligibility before exposing a cloned affected-material DTO. Missing or invalid material fails closed and Canvas must not infer impact from review-cockpit actions, feedback affordances, widget bindings, semantic overlays, or array order. React may display only the validated items. No execution, persistence, provider/storage/runtime/credential authority, WorkItem mutation, graph mutation, or new export path is authorized.
rationale: QA found that labeling all review-cockpit target refs as repair-affected could misrepresent unrelated follow-ups as impact evidence. Explicit host-admitted affected material makes the roadmap's why-and-what-changed UI truthful while preserving Canvas as a display and typed-intent host.

layer: L6 / Canvas M9 production-data capability and query-intent focused boundary
question: How may Canvas expose a production data-source capability, request a query, and display host route/admission results without owning SQL, provider runtimes, credentials, routing, approval, or execution?
decision: Canvas may add a focused-subpath-only @graphrefly/canvas/workspace-production-data public surface containing bounded data-only host-derived source capability/profile views, bounded executor capability views, immutable query-plan refs, caller-owned typed query intents, correlated route/admission result views, pure builders/validators, and inert eligibility output. The package root must not expand. Query intents carry caller-supplied intentId and idempotencyKey plus exact source/profile/query-plan refs and immutable revisions; they must not carry raw SQL, connection strings, credentials, tokens, env vars, filesystem paths, arbitrary argv/commands, provider/runtime clients or handles, callbacks, promises, opaque cursors, raw ExecutorRoute/ExecutorOutcome material, or executable values. Canvas does not produce canonical ExecutorRoute, admission decisions, executable run requests, retries, fallback, approvals, or outcomes. The host and GraphReFly runtime own source truth, route production, profile binding, admission, idempotency/deduplication, credentials, policy enforcement, execution, cancellation, evidence, audit persistence, and downstream effects. Exact source/profile/query-plan/revision/request/route/admission correlation, compatibility, and fail-closed action eligibility live in one compact private named @graphrefly/ts graph boundary under D596, with stable graph/topologyGroup/node names, topology()/describe() evidence, and idempotent release; catalog rows, forms, panel models, summaries, provenance packaging, and React rendering remain DTO-only. Canvas consumes bounded projections rather than exposing raw open-ended ExecutorProfile/ExecutorRoute/ExecutorOutcome metadata or result material. M10 should first reuse the existing GraphReFly tool executor, open inputKind/schemaRef, ToolProviderCatalog, adapter runtime, and visible run-admission facts. A new executor kind, generic data-source substrate fact, route/admission semantic, credential/runtime binding, or Canvas-owned provider registry requires a later design review and durable decision; data-specific core verbs are not authorized by this decision.
rationale: D213, D359-D361, D416, and D419 already provide provider-neutral executor, route, adapter-runtime, and visible admission authority while keeping clients and secrets private. D505/D519/D555 permit Canvas to display readiness and emit typed SQL/query requests but do not define a caller-consumable production-data surface or exact source/profile/query-plan correlation. A focused bounded projection avoids leaking open-ended runtime facts into the browser, while D596 keeps authority-sensitive eligibility graph-visible. Reusing the existing tool-provider path lets M9 unlock M10 without prematurely adding data-specific substrate primitives or a parallel Canvas runtime.

layer: L6 / PostgreSQL-compatible Layer C adapter and Canvas M10 vertical
question: How may the first certified PostgreSQL-compatible source-to-answer path reuse GraphReFly tool-provider execution while keeping SQL resolution, credentials, clients, pools, cancellation, version rollout, and execution authority outside Canvas and graph DATA?
decision: The first PostgreSQL-compatible read-only query adapter reuses the existing Layer C tool-provider path without a new protocol verb, executor kind, inputKind family, generic data-source fact, route/admission semantic, database DSL, or Canvas provider registry. The public execution input remains inputKind tool-call with a target-specific PostgreSQL query tool/operation and versioned argument/result schemaRefs. Its bounded arguments carry only the D601 admitted immutable query-plan, source, source-profile, executor-profile, and schema coordinates plus bounded parameter material or refs; raw SQL is resolved only by the host-private plan resolver beside the runtime binding and never enters the Canvas intent, Canvas DTOs, graph descriptions, snapshots, audit material, or public bounded request contract. A concrete PostgreSQL-compatible catalog and async runtime may live only on a focused @graphrefly/ts executor-adapter surface. Existing ToolProviderCatalog/Profile/ExecutionPolicy, ExecutorRoute, adapter-input, explicit D419 run-admission, visible run/attempt, ExecutorOutcome, status, issues, usage, audit, and artifact/material-ref facts remain canonical graph truth. The host owns D601-intent-to-tool-call lowering, request/operation/run identities, exact correlation, query-plan admission and dereference, route production, admission, idempotency/deduplication, retry request production, artifact persistence, and downstream effects. Runtime-private injected bindings own credential resolution, driver/client/pool/transaction/AbortController handles and enforce read-only execution, statement/connection timeout, row/column/cell/inline/result-byte bounds, redaction, and checked-out-client release. Runtime-owned pools are closed on idempotent dispose after active work is cooperatively canceled and retained private state is cleared; explicitly caller-owned shared pools are never closed by the runtime. Hidden route selection, fallback, approval, retry, query replay, adapter-version switching, or driver-level statement retry is forbidden. User cancellation is an exact-run-correlated graph-visible request and admission path; runtime shutdown/timeout cancellation alone does not stand in for user cancellation, and Canvas never receives a private cancel callback or AbortController. Adapter identity, semantic adapterVersion, driver compatibility, support tier, limitations, and rollout cohort are graph-visible catalog/profile/run provenance. Rollout or rollback uses a new visible profile/route/run pinned to the selected version, never a hidden runtime switch. Provider outcomes classify authentication or credential posture, authorization/read-only violation, connectivity, server/resource limit, timeout, cancellation, schema drift or incompatible plan, malformed/unsafe plan, result/artifact limit failure, adapter/driver mismatch, and provider-unknown failure with explicit retryability; any retry is a new visible run request and is re-admitted where required. Canvas may extend only its focused workspace-production-data surface with bounded allowlisted host-derived adapter catalog/readiness/outcome/answer-preview DTOs, typed follow-up intents, and pure React rendering. Canvas summaries are derived DTOs or explicitly labeled fallback overlays; real request-to-outcome topology remains the GraphReFly graph. M10 may use one host-selected explicit execution environment and display its locality, but environment target selection, cross-environment promotion, worker/control-plane transport, queue, heartbeat, and deployment ontology remain M11 decisions.
rationale: D213, D359-D361, D416, and D419 already define provider-neutral tool execution, runtime-private clients and credentials, visible run attempts, explicit admission, bounded outcomes, and no hidden retry or fallback. D601 adds the Canvas production-data intent and exact correlation floor while explicitly reserving concrete credential/runtime bindings for later review. A target-specific PostgreSQL adapter is the smallest reusable certified vertical: a host-private proof would not satisfy the M10 reusable pack, while a generic database registry or new executor/input ontology would prematurely expand substrate authority. Pinning plan coordinates, resource ownership, cancellation, bounds, failures, and adapter versions makes the real side-effect lifecycle inspectable without placing SQL, secrets, clients, pools, or execution authority in Canvas or graph DATA.

layer: L6 / execution-environment targeting and Canvas M11 vertical
question: How may one admitted business/query intent execute through local, GraphReFly-managed, or customer-hosted environments without creating parallel routing semantics, replaying admission, hiding queue/session lifecycle, moving credentials into graph DATA, or granting Canvas runtime authority?
decision: M11 keeps D213 ExecutorProfile and ExecutorRoute as the only executor capability and target-selection ontology. It does not add an EnvironmentRoute, generic environment selector/registry, new executor kind, remote ordinary graph dependency, or Dispatcher WorkerPool backend. Each routable executor profile pins a bounded immutable execution-environment identity and revision plus locality, capability, limit, policy, readiness/freshness, and attestation refs; each ExecutorRoute and executable run is exactly correlated to request, operation, input, executor, profile, environment identity/revision, run, and attempt. Local-process/container, GraphReFly-managed-cloud, and customer-hosted-outbound bindings use the same provider-neutral adapter-input, explicit D419 admission, run/status, ExecutorOutcome, ExecutorUsage, issue, and audit contracts. Environment is an authorization condition: promotion or environment change preserves business/query/spec identity but produces a new environment-pinned profile/route/run and a new admission with sourceRefs to the prior evidence; an old admission or run is never moved, relabeled, replayed, or silently resumed. Local bindings may consume an admitted run directly. Remote bindings use explicit application-layer request/response session envelopes and central queue/lease/attempt composition consistent with D130-D134 and existing work-queue semantics; they are not same-wave remote deps or WorkerPool jobs. The control plane owns inventory, profile publication, route and run admission, queue ordering, lease/attempt truth, idempotency, authorization, cancellation admission, artifact references, and canonical final run status. The worker owns only its runtime-private transport, process/client/pool, credentials, execution resource, cooperative cancellation handle, and shutdown/drain. A worker validates and executes an admitted immutable envelope; it never chooses a route, changes versions, retries, falls back, promotes, or adopts unadmitted work. Queue claim, lease, session epoch, heartbeat renewal, start, bounded progress, cancel command/ack, settlement, expiration, disconnect, and stale/unverifiable evidence are graph-visible. Heartbeat renews liveness/lease only and is not progress. Disconnect or lease expiry emits lost, expired, pending, or unverifiable posture and never privately replays or resumes work. Reconnect creates a new session epoch; retry, recovery, or rerun is a new visible run/attempt and is re-admitted. Cancellation is exactly correlated to run, attempt, environment revision, and session epoch; while disconnected it remains pending/unconfirmed, and a later command is delivered only when the target attempt/session remains current. Credentials stay runtime-private in the executing environment: local credentials remain with the local host binding, managed credentials remain with the GraphReFly-managed secret binding, and customer credentials remain only at the outbound customer worker. Public data-movement policy/evidence contains only bounded allowlisted classifications, direction, size/measurement, encryption, redaction, retention, sensitivity, schema and artifact/source refs. The central queue may retain only a strict admitted request envelope plus immutable payload/artifact refs; it never stores secrets, raw SQL, clients, handles, arbitrary logs, or unrestricted provider material. Small strict wire material may cross the boundary under explicit bounds; large results, logs, artifacts, and telemetry use D270/D293 bounded summaries and immutable refs with an explicit storage owner. Hidden target fallback, retry, replay, resume, version switch, promotion, opaque cursor, or credential transfer is forbidden. Canvas may add a focused-only workspace-execution-plane surface containing bounded host-derived target catalog/readiness, route/run/status/outcome/usage/failure/audit projections and separate strict route, promotion, cancel, refresh, and detail intents. Canvas does not own inventory, registry, routing, admission, queue, lease, heartbeat, session, transport, worker, credentials, execution, promotion outcome, persistence, or graph truth. Exact target/profile/query/spec/request/route/admission/run/attempt/version correlation and fail-closed route/promotion eligibility use one compact private named graph boundary plus an inert DTO shell under D596; catalog rows, status summaries, comparisons, and rendering remain DTO-only. A fallback overlay is explicitly labeled, never treated as topology truth, and never action-enabling. The first implementation may deliver only a real local-process/container vertical, but the public contract must honestly express all three localities and must not claim managed-cloud or customer-hosted execution until their concrete bindings and lifecycle evidence exist.
rationale: D130-D134 already place runtime IO behind graph-owned drivers and visible session/wire bundles; D137-D138 separate environment work, local compute WorkerPool work, and remote graph boundaries; D213 owns executor profile/route authority; D416/D419 require explicit async run and admission facts; D270/D293 bound artifact and size evidence; and D602 deliberately deferred environment selection and promotion. Reusing those contracts preserves one execution truth while making environment authorization, queue/lease/session lifecycle, cancellation, credential residency, and movement evidence explicit. A Canvas registry, per-environment executor ontology, WireEdgeGroup-as-queue, or remote WorkerPool would duplicate authority or violate the graph causal boundary. New route/run/admission on promotion prevents hidden environment switching and makes evidence comparable without claiming identical infrastructure or bytes.

layer: L6 / concrete local-container execution binding and Canvas M11 vertical
question: How may the first local-container PostgreSQL execution path pin image and isolation identity, inject credentials, expose lifecycle and cancellation, and clean up resources without creating a generic container platform, leaking runtime-private material, or weakening D603 admission?
decision: The first local-container binding remains a concrete Layer C executor runtime under D603 and reuses ExecutorProfile, ExecutorRoute, ExecutionEnvironmentTarget, exact D419 admission, provider-neutral run/outcome/usage/issues/audit, and the existing Canvas workspace-execution-plane focused surface. It does not add a container executor kind, environment registry, generic container provider, Canvas lifecycle owner, or substrate primitive. An execution-environment revision immutably resolves through a host-owned manifest to one image content digest, engine/runtime compatibility revision, typed workload recipe revision, sandbox revision, mount/network/resource policy revisions, and attestation. Mutable image tags, implicit image entrypoints, engine auto-update, hidden pull, hidden retry, hidden fallback, container reuse, checkpoint/resume, and orphan adoption are forbidden. Public and graph-visible material contains only bounded immutable digest/manifest/policy/capability/limit/readiness/attestation coordinates and refs; raw command, argv, environment variables, host paths, mount sources, daemon/socket endpoints, registry or workload credentials, engine clients, container IDs/handles, and unrestricted logs remain runtime-private. The v1 workload is one typed PostgreSQL read-only query recipe; its host-private manifest derives the concrete entrypoint/argv and may not inherit or accept arbitrary caller commands. The runtime-private local container driver is host-injected and exposes bounded prepare/create/start/wait/stop/kill/remove lifecycle operations; the first certified implementation may support one explicitly named compatibility family and must not claim Docker, Podman, Kubernetes, or other engines are interchangeable without tests. Readiness proves engine reachability and compatibility, exact image digest presence/verification, recipe and isolation-policy revision, required isolation capabilities, quota/resource posture, artifact resolver posture, and credential resolver posture with freshness/attestation; daemon ping alone is insufficient. V1 isolation defaults are read-only root filesystem, non-root, dropped capabilities, no-new-privileges, bounded CPU/memory/pids/time/result movement, deny-by-default network, no privileged mode, no host network, no engine socket, and no host bind mounts except admission-pinned immutable artifact/workspace refs resolved to private paths by the host. Secret values remain in the local host/container runtime; v1 forbids ordinary environment-variable secret injection and uses a controlled ephemeral secret mount or engine-secret equivalent that is destroyed during cleanup. Pull/create/start/execute/stop/kill/wait/remove transitions and failures are observable through bounded canonical run status, phase detail, issues, audit, usage, movement summaries, and immutable artifact refs without creating a second final-status authority. Image preparation is pre-admission readiness truth in v1; a missing or mismatched digest fails closed and is not pulled after admission. Each admitted attempt receives a fresh bounded container binding/session epoch; cancellation is exactly correlated to run, attempt, environment revision, manifest fingerprint, and epoch, first requests cooperative stop for a policy-pinned grace period, then kill, and never targets a newer attempt. Cancellation acknowledgement and final settlement are distinct; terminal provider outcome is established only after wait and cleanup. Every terminal, error, cancellation, and dispose path attempts remove and ephemeral-secret/network/temp cleanup exactly once with idempotent retry-safe ownership. Cleanup failure is independently visible and makes cleanup/attestation posture failed or unverifiable without deleting or rewriting the provider outcome. Daemon loss, unexpected exit, cleanup failure, stale attestation, quota/policy mismatch, or unverifiable evidence never privately resumes work; recovery is a new visible run or attempt and is re-admitted. Stdout/stderr, inspect events, and raw engine errors do not enter canonical DATA; only bounded redacted summaries with byte/truncation evidence and immutable artifact refs under explicit storage/retention ownership may appear. Canvas may add discriminated allowlisted local-container target/run detail for image verification, runtime/readiness, isolation, quota, limitations, phase, cleanup, usage, movement, issues and audit, but it remains an inert host-derived DTO shell and reuses the existing private exact eligibility graph. Local direct queue, lease, remote session, and heartbeat remain not-applicable. Local-process behavior remains unchanged; managed-cloud and customer-hosted execution remain unclaimed.
rationale: D603 fixes the shared environment authorization and ownership model but intentionally does not define a concrete container engine, immutable image identity, isolation, credential injection, cancellation escalation, cleanup, or attestation contract. A narrow host-injected driver plus immutable manifest keeps engine and secret material private while making admission, lifecycle, failures, cancellation, cleanup and movement evidence inspectable. Digest pinning and pre-admission readiness prevent hidden image mutation or pulling; deny-by-default isolation and ephemeral secret handling prevent the browser or graph from becoming a raw container control plane. Reusing the existing executor, admission, outcome and Canvas contracts preserves one execution truth and avoids a generic registry or second lifecycle ontology.

layer: L6 / concrete GraphReFly-managed PostgreSQL worker and Canvas M11 vertical
question: How may the first managed-cloud PostgreSQL worker use a durable queue, lease, session transport, credentials, cancellation, reconnect, and settlement without creating a generic cloud platform, weakening D419, replaying work, or granting Canvas control-plane authority?
decision: The first managed-cloud binding is one concrete GraphReFly-managed PostgreSQL read-only worker family under D603. It reuses D213 ExecutorProfile/ExecutorRoute, ExecutionEnvironmentTarget, exact D419 admission, existing WorkQueue command/record lifecycle, D133/D134-style application session envelopes, provider-neutral run/status/outcome/usage/issues/audit, and the existing Canvas workspace-execution-plane focused surface. It does not add a generic managed-provider registry, environment ontology, remote WorkerPool, ordinary remote graph dependency, or second queue/final-status authority. A host-injected PostgreSQL control-store driver, pinned to one named schema and server compatibility family, executes parameterized atomic compare-and-set transactions and owns strict admitted-run envelope persistence, idempotency, queue ordering, claim, lease/attempt truth, worker/session authorization, cancellation admission, and canonical settlement; existing in-memory WorkQueue and WireBridge implementations are semantic composition aids and tests, not claims of durable distributed persistence. The first worker initiates an outbound authenticated WSS-over-TLS connection to the managed control plane. Public graph material uses a strict typed bounded request/response session protocol; WSS URLs, TLS/auth material, decoded raw frames, transport handles, timers, clients, credentials, SQL, provider errors, and artifact resolver handles remain runtime-private. Connection identity and execution session epoch are distinct. Every reconnect creates a new epoch and never automatically replays a command, restores a lease, resumes execution, adopts an attempt, retries, changes version, falls back to local execution, or reuses the local-container binding. A claim/lease binds work, request, route, admission, run, attempt, environment identity/revision, deployment fingerprint, worker identity/revision, and session epoch. Heartbeat renews only liveness and lease; it is never progress, completion, or provider outcome. Worker settlement is bounded evidence. The control plane accepts it as canonical outcome only for the current exact lease, attempt, worker, environment revision, deployment fingerprint, and epoch; stale, duplicate, disconnected, expired, or mismatched settlement is rejected visibly. Lease expiry or disconnect produces lost, expired, pending-unconfirmed, or unverifiable truth and never privately resumes work. Automatic WorkQueue retry is disabled. Recovery, retry, rerun, failover, version change, or promotion requires a new visible run/attempt, route as applicable, and D419 admission. Cancellation is separately proposed and admitted with exact work, lease, run, attempt, environment revision, deployment fingerprint, worker revision, and session epoch. Delivery acknowledgement is not outcome. Disconnected cancellation remains pending-unconfirmed; an old-epoch command may not be rebound after reconnect, and a newly current epoch requires a new exact cancellation admission. Provider credentials exist only inside the managed worker through short-lived workload identity and managed secret binding. Queue, graph DATA, public session envelopes, Canvas, logs, and artifacts never contain credential values, connection strings, secret environment, clients, handles, endpoints, or signed URLs. The queue stores only an immutable bounded admitted envelope plus strict artifact/source refs and allowlisted coordinates; raw SQL, large results, arbitrary logs, provider responses, unrestricted metadata, and opaque cursors are forbidden. Data movement exposes only bounded schema/classification, measured bytes, encryption, redaction, retention, sensitivity, storage-owner, artifact, and source refs; large material remains behind immutable D270/D293 refs. The focused @graphrefly/ts managed-cloud PostgreSQL surface may define strict deployment/readiness facts, admitted dispatch envelope, queue/lease/session/cancel/settlement facts, pure validators/projectors, and a host-injected runtime bundle. Package root remains unchanged. Canvas may add only discriminated allowlisted managed-cloud target/run detail and exact route/cancel/detail intents, reusing the existing compact private eligibility graph. Canvas never owns inventory, queue, lease, session, transport, worker, credential, settlement, retry, or persistence authority. Customer-hosted endpoint enrollment, tenant-controlled transport, worker distribution/update, customer credential residency, firewall/proxy policy, customer attestation, offline buffering, and cross-domain trust remain unclaimed and require a separate decision.
rationale: D603 fixes the shared environment and remote-session ownership model but does not choose a concrete managed worker family, durable store boundary, transport direction, reconnect behavior, credential delivery, settlement admission, or retry policy. Existing WorkQueue and WireBridge supply reusable lifecycle vocabulary but are intentionally in-memory/generic and cannot honestly be relabeled a durable managed control plane. A narrow host-injected durable store plus strict outbound worker session makes queue, lease, liveness, cancellation, and settlement testable while retaining runtime-private transport and provider material. Disabling implicit replay/retry and requiring exact epoch/lease settlement preserves D419 and one canonical execution truth without prematurely generalizing into customer-hosted execution.

layer: L6 / concrete customer-hosted outbound PostgreSQL endpoint and Canvas M11 vertical
question: How may the first customer-hosted outbound PostgreSQL endpoint enroll, receive and update a worker, retain customer credentials, traverse proxy and firewall boundaries, attest identity/readiness, handle offline/disconnect, cancel, and settle across administrative domains without creating generic fleet/runtime authority or hidden replay?
decision: The first customer-hosted binding is one concrete PostgreSQL read-only endpoint-agent family under D603. It reuses D213 ExecutorProfile/ExecutorRoute, ExecutionEnvironmentTarget, exact D419 admission, provider-neutral run/status/outcome/usage/issues/audit, and central PostgreSQL-16 atomic queue/lease/fence/cancellation/settlement semantics, but it is a separate focused authority from D605 managed workers and does not generalize managed credentials, enrollment, trust, or transport. A customer explicitly installs one GraphReFly-published signed and sha256-digest-pinned OCI agent revision for the first linux/amd64 compatibility family. The agent verifies publisher signature, SBOM/provenance refs, digest, recipe, sandbox, and update-policy revisions. It never self-updates, follows a mutable channel, downgrades, rolls back, hot-swaps, adopts, or resumes an admitted run. Install/update/rollback requires explicit customer action and a new visible endpoint/agent revision, environment profile/route/run and D419 admission; the old revision drains without hidden fallback. Enrollment is control-plane authorized, tenant/environment scoped, and uses one single-use short-lived bootstrap grant over outbound TLS only to prove possession and activate one endpoint identity, enrollment revision, and key generation. TOFU, reusable bootstrap secrets, and Canvas-created tokens are forbidden. The control plane persists only bounded tenant/endpoint/enrollment/key-generation/agent digest+revision/trust/policy/credential-binding coordinates, certificate/public-key fingerprints and revocation truth; bootstrap values, private keys, certificate handles, endpoint addresses, hostnames/IPs, proxy URLs/auth, device inventory, and TLS handles remain runtime-private. Rotation or re-enrollment creates a new visible enrollment/key generation; revocation blocks sessions/claims and terminates eligibility without erasing history. The endpoint agent alone initiates authenticated mTLS WSS over TLS 1.3 through customer-approved outbound 443/proxy policy. No inbound listener, polling fallback, callback URL, VPN, tunnel, arbitrary transport/plugin registry, remote ordinary graph dependency, WorkerPool, or Canvas transport is authorized. Every reconnect creates a fresh session epoch; old epochs are tombstoned and never replay, restore, resume, adopt, retry, renew, settle, or receive rebound cancellation. The central control plane remains sole inventory/profile publication, route/admission, durable queue ordering, idempotency, attempt/lease/fence, cancellation admission, and canonical final-status authority. Exact claim/message/cancel/settlement correlation includes tenant, endpoint identity+revision, enrollment/key generation, agent digest+revision, environment/deployment revision+fingerprint, work/queue attempt, lease/fence, worker assignment, protocol/recipe/policy revisions, run/attempt, and session epoch. Heartbeat is liveness only. The agent owns only private transport, customer credential resolver/handles, PostgreSQL client/pool, process/execution resource, and cooperative local stop. It never chooses routes, promotes, retries, replays, resumes, adopts, mints attempts, extends leases offline, or declares canonical settlement. Customer PostgreSQL DSN/password/certs remain solely in a customer-owned file/socket/secret resolver; ordinary environment secret injection and central secret transfer are forbidden. Queue, graph DATA, session envelopes, Canvas, logs, and artifacts contain no credential value, endpoint/proxy detail, raw SQL, rows, clients, handles, unrestricted logs/provider errors, or signed URLs. Attestation exposes only bounded signed software/config/key-possession/proxy-firewall/policy posture and evidence refs; it proves identity/integrity/posture, not hardware/TEE/compliance, host correctness, provider truth, or secret non-exfiltration. Readiness requires current non-revoked enrollment/key generation, exact signed agent digest/revision, current attestation, outbound policy posture, central store/schema/quota/artifact readiness, and customer-local credential resolver readiness. Missing, stale, revoked, mismatched, disconnected, or unverifiable evidence fails closed. Disconnect immediately fences the lease, cooperatively stops then closes local execution, and emits lost/expired/pending-unconfirmed/unverifiable posture; execution occurrence may remain unverifiable and exactly-once distributed execution is not claimed. Recovery always requires a new admitted run/attempt. Cancellation is separately persisted and admitted on every exact coordinate; ack is receipt only, disconnected cancel remains pending-unconfirmed, and an old command is never rebound. A customer local emergency stop is bounded noncanonical evidence, not central cancel admission or outcome. No offline work, command, claim, lease renewal, start, result queue, retry, or canonical settlement is allowed. The only offline persistence is one customer-owned bounded encrypted evidence outbox with finite entry/byte/age policy and fail-closed full/key-unavailable posture. It may retain exact IDs, timestamps, terminal posture, and bounded issue/source/artifact refs only—never workload, SQL, rows, secrets, provider errors, or cancel commands. Upload after reconnect is noncanonical audit evidence; it cannot renew/rebind an epoch, settle an old attempt, or trigger replay. Outbox queued/uploaded/rejected/expired/explicit-policy-drop lifecycle is visible and cleanup is endpoint-owned. Data movement is direction/classification/schema/bytes/encryption/redaction/retention/sensitivity/storage-owner policy admitted. Small strict result material or immutable D270/D293 refs may cross; customer-local refs are not claimed centrally retrievable/immutable without bounded attestation. The first focused @graphrefly/ts customer-hosted PostgreSQL surface may define strict enrollment/release/readiness/envelope/lease/session/cancel/settlement/outbox facts, concrete central CAS adapter, explicit enrollment/trust verifier, outbound transport and customer-local worker runtime. Package root remains closed. Canvas may add only strict discriminated customer-hosted target/run/outbox DTOs and exact route/cancel/refresh/detail intents, reusing its existing private 2-node/1-edge eligibility graph. Canvas owns no enrollment token, inventory, certificate/key, agent distribution/update, endpoint address, queue/session/credential/runtime/settlement/persistence authority, and fallback overlays remain inert. Generic fleet management, Kubernetes/operator support, multi-platform agents, hardware attestation, arbitrary workloads/databases/transports, customer-hosted control plane/queue, multi-endpoint failover, offline execution, secret sync, raw result/log transport, and managed-to-customer fallback remain unclaimed.
rationale: D603 defines shared remote execution ownership and D605 proves a managed control plane, but customer-hosted execution crosses a separate administrative and credential boundary. Reusing the managed worker by relabeling locality would falsely unify enrollment, software supply chain, proxy/firewall, customer credential residency, attestation and offline ambiguity. A narrow signed endpoint agent with outbound-only authenticated sessions, central fenced authority, customer-local credentials, severe disconnect semantics and a noncanonical evidence-only outbox makes the boundary testable without inventing a generic fleet platform or claiming exactly-once execution across partitions.

layer: L6 / governed PostgreSQL production-run operations and Canvas M12 vertical
question: How may users diagnose a failed, stale, partial, timed-out, blocked, or unverifiable PostgreSQL production run and request retry, rerun, replay/backfill, repair, rollback, resume, cancellation, or a support bundle without turning Canvas into recovery authority, collapsing distinct semantics, mutating old runs, or weakening D419 and M11 fencing?
decision: The first M12 vertical is one concrete governed PostgreSQL production-run operations family over the M9-M11 trusted-data-query journey. It reuses exact D419 admission, D602 PostgreSQL execution, D603-D606 environment and fencing authority, D505/D519/D555 host-derived display plus typed-intent boundaries, D270/D293 artifact refs, D358 proposal-based repair, and D596 exact-correlation graph eligibility. It does not create a generic recovery provider, command registry, incident ontology, workflow engine, callback resume mechanism, or substrate protocol verb. A host-owned PostgreSQL-16-compatible append-only/CAS recovery ledger in a separate named schema is the sole canonical authority for recovery request recording, idempotency, access/admission decision, materialization, terminal recovery status, successor correlation, ordered audit refs, and expiry. Canvas and ordinary Graph DATA never own or reconstruct this ledger. Recovery identity is caller-supplied intentId/idempotencyKey plus tenant/workspace, action kind, and an exact immutable target tuple. Matching key and canonical body re-reference the existing record; the same key with different material is an explicit conflict. Admission and materialization recheck current terminal/high-water truth and exact request, operation, route, admission, run, attempt, outcome, executor/profile, environment/deployment, query/spec/input/source/schema/artifact, policy, retention and evidence coordinates as applicable; stale, missing, ambiguous, unauthorized, mismatched, expired, inaccessible, retention-gap, unverifiable-execution, or conflicting material fails closed. Recovery never mutates, relabels, reopens, resumes, erases, or replaces the prior run/outcome/admission. Retry means a new explicit attempt/run over the same immutable admitted input only when policy and occurrence evidence make that safe; rerun means a new run request and always receives new route/admission/run/attempt coordinates as applicable. Both pass through the ordinary exact D419 admission path and retain immutable sourceRefs to the prior run and recovery record. Replay/backfill is a distinct action, never an alias for retry: it is eligible only from an exact retained immutable source snapshot plus explicit bounded range/window, schema/spec/policy/retention coordinates and dedupe material, and it creates a new request/run through D419. Missing retention proof, a live or mutable cursor, opaque provider cursor, inaccessible snapshot, or unverifiable source boundary makes replay/backfill ineligible. Resume is explicitly unsupported in this vertical because M11 owns no durable compatible execution checkpoint; reconnect, lease renewal, retry, replay and adoption must never be described as resume. Generic rollback is explicitly unsupported. Any future rollback requires a resource-specific compensating proposal and owner; committed graph waves, WorkQueue history, prior effects, outcomes, artifacts and external provider state are not rewound. Repair may only emit a bounded typed proposal referencing exact evidence and then follows D358/WorkItem proposal, admission and application authority; recovery admission itself cannot mutate WorkItems, graph truth, source state, artifacts or provider state. Exact cancellation reuses D603-D606 action-specific current attempt/lease/fence/session semantics and remains separate from recovery success; acknowledgement is not outcome. Production incident assignment, acknowledgement, notes, severity changes and resolution truth are deferred to a separate incident-ledger decision and may appear only as host-derived display material or typed request shells here. Operational inspection exposes bounded host-derived history, progress, failure class, freshness/quality, lineage, usage/cost, movement, outcome, issue, audit, artifact/evidence and retention/access posture. Missing-input, request-admission failure, runtime failure, partial output, stale evidence, retention gap, access restriction and unverifiable execution occurrence remain distinct and may not collapse into one unavailable or retryable flag. Recovery eligibility is action-specific with explicit reason, required evidence, access/admission posture and exact coordinate pins; no generic retryable boolean enables an action. The first focused @graphrefly/ts PostgreSQL run-operations surface may define strict recovery request/admission/record/materialization/successor/comparison facts, the concrete host-injected PostgreSQL CAS adapter, pure validators/projectors and a bridge that derives new D419 candidate requests without executing them. Package root remains closed. Canvas may add a focused workspace-run-operations surface containing strict inert operational history, diagnosis, action-eligibility, recovery-intent, host-admission/outcome, before/after evidence-comparison and support-bundle request DTOs. Exact target correlation, immutable handoff validation, conflict material and fail-closed eligibility live in one compact private named graph boundary; the intended first budget is five nodes and no more than six edges for admitted source state, exact correlation, diagnosis, action eligibility and evidence comparison. Rows, logs, cost/usage summaries, support-bundle summaries and rendering remain DTO-only. Real runtime/WorkGraph topology is primary truth; incident paths are labeled semantic overlays and cannot replace or infer graph truth. The Canvas package root remains unchanged. A bounded redacted support bundle is assembled, authorized, stored, retained, signed and downloaded only by the host. Canvas may display a bounded summary and immutable artifact/evidence refs and emit an idempotent typed export/request-detail intent, but it never carries raw SQL, rows, full logs, stack traces, source excerpts, credentials, endpoints, signed URLs, clients, sockets, handles, opaque cursors or unrestricted metadata. Hosts own actor/capability/policy authorization for inspect, request, admit, execute, cancel and export; admission pending/denied/expired remains distinct from runtime outcome, and Canvas never shows optimistic recovery success.
rationale: M11 proves four concrete execution localities but deliberately requires every recovery to be a new visible admitted run and forbids hidden retry, replay, resume, adoption and fallback. D505/D519/D555 allow operational DTOs and typed intents, while D596 requires exact recovery eligibility to remain graph-inspectable, but none defines a durable recovery lifecycle, action-specific semantics, persistence, fencing, access, audit or successor correlation. A narrow PostgreSQL recovery ledger plus compact Canvas eligibility graph makes the first production failure-to-recovery journey testable without turning WorkQueue, WorkItems, runtime adapters or Canvas into a universal recovery engine. Keeping retry, replay/backfill, repair, resume, rollback and cancel semantically separate preserves evidence quality and prevents missing input, retention gaps or unverifiable execution from becoming unsafe reruns.

layer: L6 / restricted recurring PostgreSQL shared control panel and Canvas M13 vertical
question: How may a validated PostgreSQL investigation become a durable restricted shared control panel with separately admitted view, rerun, download, input, subscription and action affordances, recurring query occurrences, stale/anomaly alerts and inbox delivery without copying Workspace/WorkGraph truth or granting Canvas persistence, permission, scheduler, delivery or runtime authority?
decision: The first M13 vertical is one concrete restricted PostgreSQL trusted-query control-panel family over the M9-M12 journey. It reuses D538 widget composition, D539 binding descriptors, D519/D555 typed-intent and host-derived display boundaries, D564/D565 real graph topology authority, D596 compact exact-correlation eligibility, exact D419 run admission, D607 operational evidence/recovery, and D270/D293 immutable artifact/evidence refs. It does not create a generic artifact registry, RBAC/ACL platform, scheduler, notification provider, action plugin registry, incident ontology, collaborative authoring system, or substrate protocol verb. A host-owned PostgreSQL-16-compatible control-panel authority is the sole canonical persistence owner. A panel has stable tenant/workspace/panel identity and immutable panel revisions. Each revision binds the same exact WorkGraph identity/revision/topology fingerprint and contains presentation intent only: ordered widget ids, bounded layout frames, strict widget/binding/display descriptors, and immutable refs to exact query/spec/input/source/schema/run/attempt/outcome/evidence/artifact/freshness material. It never copies answer rows, outcome truth, graph topology, permission truth, runtime state, credentials or provider material. Create/save appends a revision and advances one mutable head through CAS over expectedHeadRevision. Matching idempotency key and canonical body rereferences the prior result; the same key with different body is conflict. Stale heads never last-write-win, auto-merge, silently fork or overwrite. Reopen resolves a host-admitted head to one exact revision; opening history is a distinct intent. Underlying WorkGraph/run changes do not mutate saved pins: stale, missing, restricted or mismatched bindings remain visible and require an explicitly admitted new revision. A restricted share/view is a host-derived projection of the same admitted panel revision, never a copied Workspace, forked graph or second panel truth. The host alone owns actor/session identity, tenant/workspace membership, subject/group resolution, grant/capability truth, policy evaluation/revision, redaction profile, share admission, revocation/expiry, retention, idempotency, audit and effect materialization. Every projection and effect pins tenant/workspace, panelId/revision, WorkGraph identity/revision/topology fingerprint, relevant query/spec/input/source/schema/run/attempt/outcome/evidence high-water, actor identity/session revision, grant/capability-set revision, policy revision, redaction profile revision, intent/idempotency, issued/expiry and admission revision. Current coordinates are rechecked at materialization and delivery; cached Canvas posture is never authority. Revocation or expiry immediately blocks new projection, occurrence, action and delivery admission while preserving append-only panel/share/run/alert/audit history. Redaction is applied by the host before Canvas and is monotonic for a restricted projection; Canvas cannot hydrate, join, infer or reveal suppressed material or downgrade a redaction profile. View, query-rerun, download, input, subscribe and action are six independent fail-closed capability postures and admissions, never one canAccess boolean. View yields only a bounded redacted projection and exact drill refs. Query-rerun creates a new ordinary M9/M10/D419 request/run within explicitly admitted query/spec/input/source scope and never mutates or reopens an old run. Download only requests a host-packaged/stored/authorized artifact and never carries signed URLs, bytes, paths or storage handles. Input only submits bounded schema-pinned input material to an exact admitted slot/revision and never carries arbitrary properties, SQL or credentials. Subscribe only requests the concrete recurring-query family defined below. Action is an action-specific typed handoff such as D607 recovery/cancel/repair and never a generic command/callback registry. View never implies any other capability; query, input or action never implies authoring, save, share or administration. The first executable vertical supports view, query-rerun, subscribe, exact drillback and one host-owned in-product inbox delivery family. Download, input and arbitrary action remain distinct visible unsupported or denied postures in v1 rather than being collapsed into view/query or silently implemented. A separate host-owned concrete subscription/occurrence CAS authority stores immutable subscription revisions for one fixed-interval recurring PostgreSQL query family. A revision pins exact panel/query/spec/input/source/schema/environment/policy/freshness coordinates, interval, host-clock schedule anchor, enabled/suspended/expired posture, dedupe and noise policy refs, and expiry. Schedule changes create a new revision and fence future old-revision occurrences. A host-injected scheduler boundary supplies current host time; Canvas owns no timer, watcher, cron, callback, outbox or generic scheduler API. Each due occurrence is uniquely keyed by tenant, panel, subscription, subscription revision and scheduledFor. Occurrence creation is atomic and rechecks current panel/share/capability/policy/source/freshness high-water; duplicates rereference, differing material conflicts, and stale/revoked/expired/missing/mismatched/unverifiable state fails closed. Every accepted occurrence materializes a fresh ordinary M9/M10/D419 request/run; it is never checkpoint resume, old-run replay, hidden retry, lease adoption or provider-owned recurrence. A separate host-owned concrete alert evaluation authority supports one stale-or-anomaly condition family over the canonical completed occurrence outcome and evidence. Condition revisions pin bounded freshness threshold or bounded scalar anomaly comparator material; they are not arbitrary expressions, SQL, code, callbacks or a generic rules DSL. Alert identity/dedupe binds subscription revision, occurrence, condition revision and canonical evidence fingerprint. Duplicate evaluation rereferences; differing material conflicts. Cooldown, rate cap, quiet/noise policy and suppression revision are host policy facts. Suppressed/coalesced/expired evaluations remain visible records and never delete or rewrite alerts. Evaluation rechecks exact occurrence/run/outcome/source/evidence/high-water and cannot infer truth from logs or missing data. A separate host-owned concrete in-product inbox delivery authority creates one bounded delivery record from an admitted alert and exact actor/audience capability. Delivery states are pending, attempted, delivered, failed, suppressed or expired and remain separate from alert evaluation and run outcome; delivery acknowledgement is not alert truth, incident acknowledgement or provider outcome. No email, webhook, SMS, external recipient address, channel credential, retry daemon or generic notification provider is authorized. Every panel revision, share/grant decision, capability admission, subscription revision, occurrence, D419 materialization, alert evaluation, suppression and delivery transition has ordered append-only host audit refs. Canvas receives only bounded audit summaries/refs and may not claim audit merely because it rendered a view. Ordinary operators receive only the admitted redacted panel and independently admitted affordances. They never receive panel/workspace authoring, layout save/share/grant/admin, credentials, source/provider/runtime/queue/storage/policy handles, renderer registries, callbacks, raw SQL/rows/logs, opaque cursors, signed URLs, WorkItem/graph mutation or current-view ownership. Drillback is exact bounded navigation to existing WorkGraph node/run/source/evidence refs and does not hydrate or query authority. The first focused @graphrefly/ts shared-control-panel PostgreSQL surface may define strict panel/share/capability/subscription/occurrence/condition/alert/delivery facts, concrete host-injected PostgreSQL CAS adapters, pure validators/projectors and bridges that emit ordinary D419 candidates without executing them. Package root remains closed. Canvas may add a focused workspace-shared-control-panel surface containing strict inert panel/revision/layout/widget/binding, restricted projection, independent capability posture, recurring subscription/occurrence, alert/suppression/delivery, drillback and typed intent DTOs. Exact panel/WorkGraph/run correlation, freshness integrity and fail-closed affordance eligibility live in one compact private named graph boundary with an intended budget of six meaningful nodes and no more than eight edges. Layout, widget rows, alert rows, schedule/freshness summaries, audit/delivery summaries, breadcrumbs and rendering remain DTO-only. Real graph.topology()/describe() and canonical run/outcome facts remain primary truth; panel and alert paths are labeled semantic overlays. Canvas package root remains unchanged. Anonymous/public links, cross-tenant shares, external identity/SCIM, delegated/org-wide role ontology, row-level policy DSL, offline access, billing/seat enforcement, collaborative editing, arbitrary schedules/calendars, arbitrary alert expressions, external delivery channels, generic action plugins and persisted incident acknowledge/resolve/escalate remain unclaimed.
rationale: D538/D539/D555 permit pinned/shared display DTOs and typed intents but intentionally leave persistence, ordering, authorization, subscriptions, notification and effects host-owned. M12 now provides trustworthy exact production-run diagnosis and recovery, so M13 can close the investigation-to-recurring-operation loop only if panel identity/versioning, access TOCTOU, occurrence dedupe, alert evaluation and delivery truth are explicit. A concrete PostgreSQL panel plus fixed-interval occurrence, bounded stale/anomaly condition and in-product inbox family proves the release journey without turning Canvas into a backend or prematurely inventing generic RBAC, scheduler, notification or action platforms. Immutable panel revisions and same-WorkGraph restricted projections preserve provenance; independent capability admission and fresh D419 occurrences preserve one execution truth; separate alert and delivery ledgers prevent render, delivery or acknowledgement from becoming outcome authority.

layer: L5/L6 / host-injected client, connector, runtime and persistence adapter boundary
question: How should GraphReFly and Canvas integrate databases, ORMs, connectors and external runtimes without rebuilding their clients, fixing user schemas, leaking handles into graph DATA, or inventing a universal ORM while still preserving execution admission and durable product-state semantics?
decision: GraphReFly libraries define deterministic graph/executor lifecycle, typed request and outcome/evidence contracts, and narrow capability-specific ports; they do not own or recreate connection pools, wire protocols, query builders, ORM identity maps, transaction managers, database migrations, user business schemas, SDK transports, credential resolution or generic connector registries. A host injects its existing client, ORM, connector, repository, SDK or runtime through host-private closures, adapter factories, or capability functions. Raw clients, ORM sessions, transactions, cursors, connection strings, credentials, handles and callbacks never enter Graph DATA, Canvas DTOs, intents, fingerprints, audit bodies or public serializable contracts. `graph.producer()` is the general boundary for bringing an existing client-backed read or pure computation into reactive graph state; independently admitted or effectful work uses a typed executor/provider adapter with explicit execute, cancel, timeout, error classification, outcome, evidence and lifecycle behavior; durable cross-call product state uses a feature-specific narrow persistence port whose atomic operations express the required domain semantics. Producer recomputation must not silently dispatch external effects. Core packages must not provide a universal database/ORM abstraction or a union-style arbitrary-client API. Feature ports may require append, compare-and-advance, claim, rereference/conflict, audit or transaction capabilities, but they may not expose generic query, table, row, lock or ORM APIs. Hosts implement those capabilities using Prisma, Drizzle, TypeORM, Kysely, pg, DynamoDB, a remote service or another existing system. Optional concrete/reference adapters may map a named client or database family to a feature port, but they are replaceable, dependency-isolated, must not be package-root authority, and must not make their schema, migration system or client a requirement of the core GraphReFly or Canvas library. Canvas remains an inert consumer of host-derived DTOs and typed intents and never knows the user's database schema. D603-D608 references to concrete PostgreSQL CAS implementations are narrowed accordingly: their lifecycle, fencing, idempotency, exact-correlation and audit semantics remain locked, while the fixed SQL/schema implementation is only an optional host/reference adapter rather than the canonical library contract. M13 shared-control-panel production authority must therefore separate pure validated workflow/contracts from persistence capabilities and prove at least one host-injected client/repository implementation without placing SQL schema, DDL, client dependencies or transaction handles on the focused Canvas or core TS public surface.
rationale: GraphReFly must compose with the database and runtime infrastructure users already operate. Requiring a library-owned PostgreSQL schema or reconstructing ORM/client behavior increases dependencies, prevents adoption with existing repositories and conflates domain semantics with storage mechanics. At the same time, collapsing effectful execution into producer recomputation or replacing feature-specific atomic semantics with a lowest-common-denominator universal adapter would weaken admission, cancellation, idempotency, conflict and audit guarantees. The chosen split keeps GraphReFly responsible for deterministic lifecycle and exact domain contracts, lets hosts reuse mature clients and ORMs, and preserves host-private authority and schema ownership.

layer: L6 / production evaluation, external admission, migration-action and evidence-packet workspace
question: How may Canvas let a buyer evaluate, admit, migrate and expand a production workload from exact GraphReFly evidence without becoming security, procurement, production-policy, migration-effect, report-storage or runtime authority?
decision: The first M14 vertical is a production evaluation, external admission, migration-action and evidence-packet workspace over exact M9-M13 GraphReFly evidence. Evaluation campaigns are host-owned stable identities with immutable revisions. Each revision pins one bounded candidate adapter/runtime/version and configuration fingerprint, scenario-pack revision, criteria/threshold revision, eligible environment/data/source/schema/policy refs and exact tenant/workspace scope. Scenario executions always use ordinary D419 request, admission, run, outcome and evidence facts; the evaluation workspace never fabricates execution results, resolves a generic adapter registry or dispatches effects through producer recomputation. Results append by exact campaign/revision/scenario/run/evidence identity: matching key and canonical body rereference; the same key with different material conflicts. Deterministic threshold comparison, scenario dependency/completeness, exact candidate/version/config correlation, evidence freshness/high-water and action eligibility are graph-visible derived assessments, not production admission truth. Demo-ready, PoC-passed, production-admitted and expanded are not a Canvas-controlled enum or monotonic local state machine. They are host-admitted append-only decision/attestation records with exact scope, campaign/candidate revision, criteria/evidence high-water, actor/reviewer/admitter role refs, policy revision, issued/expiry/supersession posture, reason and audit refs. Security, legal, finance, procurement, SLA/support and production policy remain external authority; Canvas displays bounded host-derived posture and emits typed requests only. Revocation, expiry, supersession and new evidence do not delete history, and current effective posture is resolved by the host. Observe, shadow/dual-run, cutover and decommission are distinct action-specific proposal, admission, materialization and terminal-outcome lifecycles rather than a freely mutable stage field. Every action pins source and target adapter/runtime/version/config, bounded traffic/data/schema/policy/credential posture refs, prerequisites, coexistence evidence, rollback-plan revision, generation/fence, evidence high-water and idempotency identity. Real shadow, cutover, decommission and target-specific compensation execute only through typed executor/provider adapters with explicit cancellation, timeout, outcome and evidence; Canvas and graph producers do not execute them. Cutover requires fresh coexistence and rollback evidence. Decommission requires separate admission and does not imply success. Rollback is a target-specific compensating proposal and newly admitted run, never generic rewind of graph waves, WorkItems, prior effects, outcomes, artifacts or external state. D609 governs persistence: canonical libraries expose only feature-specific narrow atomic capabilities for immutable revision/result/decision/action/outcome/audit append, exact rereference/conflict and head/fence compare-and-advance. Hosts close over existing clients, ORMs, repositories, connectors or remote services privately; no schema, DDL, query/table API, transaction/client/cursor/credential handle or callback enters Graph DATA, Canvas DTOs, fingerprints, audit bodies or root exports. Evidence packets are DTO-only bounded manifests and immutable refs. Source authorization, redaction, packaging, signing, storage, retention, reproducibility and download/delivery remain host-owned; Canvas never carries raw rows/SQL/logs, source excerpts, unrestricted configuration/security/cost material, blobs, signed URLs or opaque cursors. Canvas may expose one focused workspace-production-evaluation surface containing explicit inert campaign/evidence/assessment/attestation/migration-action/packet DTOs, pure bounded display builders and typed intent constructors; package root remains closed. Graph constructors, inspectors, persistence authorities, lifecycle reducers, policy evaluators, registries, report assemblers and runtime/client handles remain internal.
